title: t18643: feat: seed draft PRs — companion files for issues without waiting on default-branch merge
body:
## Task


Add seed draft PRs: when an issue needs companion files (research notes, fixtures, plans, partial scaffolding) before a worker can start, the creating session pushes them on a seed branch and opens a draft PR marked as a seed. Dispatch must not treat the seed draft as an implementation checkpoint, and the dispatched worker must start from the seed head so the files are available immediately, without waiting for a merge to the default branch.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add seed draft PRs: when an issue needs companion files (research notes, fixtures, plans, partial scaffolding) before a worker can start, the creating session pushes them on a seed branch and opens a draft PR marked as a seed. Dispatch must not treat the seed draft as an implementation checkpoint, and the dispatched worker must start from the seed head so the files are available immediately, without waiting for a merge to the default branch.

## Why

Issue-first dispatch (previous leaf) removes the default-branch wait for self-contained issues. Issues that genuinely depend on extra files would otherwise still need a planning merge first. Today any open draft PR that references the issue is a durable checkpoint that blocks ordinary dispatch (`_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling` in `dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`), so a seed draft would freeze the issue.

## How

- New `.agents/scripts/seed-pr-helper.sh` with `open <issue>` (push current linked-worktree branch, open draft PR via `gh_create_pr` with label `seed-pr`, body marker `<!-- aidevops:seed-pr issue=N -->` and non-closing `For #N`), `find <issue> <repo>` (print same-repo seed PR number, head ref and head SHA; trusted collaborator authors only) and `supersede <issue> <repo> <new-pr>` (close the seed draft once a PR containing its head exists).
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`: exclude drafts labelled `seed-pr` (with the body marker) from the draft-checkpoint selection.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` `_dlw_precreate_worktree`: when a seed PR exists, create the worker branch with `--base origin/<seed-head-ref>`; tell the worker about the seed in its prompt context.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`: after PR creation, close a superseded seed PR whose head SHA is an ancestor of the pushed head.
- `.agents/scripts/label-sync-helper.sh`: register `seed-pr`.
- Docs: seed workflow in `.agents/reference/planning-publication-lifecycle.md` and `.agents/workflows/new-task.md`.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/seed-pr-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh
- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/label-sync-helper.sh
- .agents/reference/planning-publication-lifecycle.md
- .agents/workflows/new-task.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- An open draft PR labelled `seed-pr` with the seed marker for issue N does not produce a draft-checkpoint dedup block for N; other drafts still do.
- A worker dispatched for N with a seed PR starts from the seed head commit.
- The worker's implementation PR supersedes and closes the seed draft.
- Seeds from non-collaborator authors or fork heads are ignored.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-enumerate-blockers.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/seed-pr-helper.sh .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
```

- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. The security decisions are already made (see Context & Decisions); the worker implements a known pattern
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision: skipped. Issue-only is enough; the manual run below is the reference implementation

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-10
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** An operator onboarded a second GitHub org onto an existing self-hosted runner host. Every GitHub-side step was done by hand: GitHub App, installation, private-only runner group, verifying and copying the App key. The goal is to repeat this for any org whose private repos lack free GitHub-hosted minutes, on any server.

## What

1. A helper, `github-runner-org-helper.sh`, that automates the GitHub-side and key-handling steps of onboarding an org onto org-scoped, GitHub-App-authenticated, ephemeral self-hosted runners.
2. A runbook update that documents this org/App/JIT model as the recommended pattern.

The server-side runner implementation (systemd, rootless or DinD containers, JIT registration) stays operator-owned. The helper prepares and verifies everything that pool needs.

Subcommands (all accept `--dry-run` for mutations; none prints key material):

| Command | Behaviour |
|---------|-----------|
| `group-ensure --org ORG --name NAME [--repos all-private\|r1,r2]` | Creates the runner group if it is missing, or reconciles it if present. Sets `visibility=selected` and `allows_public_repositories=false`, and selects private non-archived repos. Must refuse any public repo, with a non-zero exit. Prints the group id and the selected repo names. |
| `verify-key --org ORG --app-id ID --secret NAME` | Signs an RS256 JWT with the App key from the aidevops secret, calls `GET /app` and checks that `id` and `owner.login` match. Then calls `GET /app/installations`, finds the installation for ORG, and checks its permissions are exactly `organization_self_hosted_runners: write`. Prints App slug, App ID, Installation ID and public-key SHA-256. |
| `push-key --secret NAME --host USER@HOST --dest PATH` | Streams the key over ssh stdin to the remote path with `umask 077` and `chmod 600`. Then compares the remote public-key SHA-256 with the local one and exits non-zero on mismatch. |
| `status --org ORG [--group NAME]` | Read-only: lists runner groups (name, visibility, public flag, repo count) and the runners in a group (name, status, busy, labels). |

## Why

Private and org repos use paid GitHub-hosted minutes. An operator with spare server capacity can run per-org ephemeral runners instead. Today, onboarding is a manual sequence with security traps:

- A runner group that allows public repos lets fork PRs run code on the server.
- A key that leaks into a transcript or a leftover temp file.
- A key that doesn't belong to the expected App.

The current runbook only describes a legacy repo-scoped pool with a registration token in an env file. It does not describe the org/App/JIT model now in production.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The security decisions are resolved: one App per org, private-only groups, no key in argv or files, fingerprint verification. The worker implements a known API pattern inside that boundary, but must choose its own JWT and error-handling structure.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/scripts/github-runner-broker-health-helper.sh:1-75` and its `usage`/`main` (`:405-436`). This is the helper skeleton to copy: `set -euo pipefail`, guarded `shared-constants.sh` source, env-var config block, `_prefix_` private functions, redacted `gh api` error classification.
- **Read first:** `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` `cmd_run_specific` (`:976-1024`). Inject a single named secret through `aidevops secret NAME -- cmd`, never through inject-all `secret run`.
- **Load only if:** you are editing the runbook: `.agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md`, whole file (381 lines).
- **Stop when:** the skeleton, the secret-injection path and the runbook insertion point are clear.

### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
# Key injection (one named secret, value arrives as an env var of the same name):
aidevops secret <ORG>_RUNNERS_APP_KEY -- github-runner-org-helper.sh _verify-key-inner ...
# or have the helper re-exec itself through that path when the env var is absent.

# JWT (RS256) without temp files, key read from env via process substitution:
#   header=$(printf '{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"}' | b64url)
#   payload=$(printf '{"iat":%d,"exp":%d,"iss":"%s"}' "$((now-60))" "$((now+300))" "$app_id" | b64url)
#   sig=$(printf '%s' "$header.$payload" | openssl dgst -sha256 -sign <(printf '%s\n' "$KEYVAR") | b64url)
#   b64url() { openssl base64 -A | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='; }

# Runner group create (needs admin:org on the gh token):
gh api -X POST orgs/ORG/actions/runner-groups -f name=NAME -f visibility=selected \
  -F allows_public_repositories=false -F 'selected_repository_ids[]=ID' ...
# Reconcile: PATCH orgs/ORG/actions/runner-groups/GID and
#            PUT  orgs/ORG/actions/runner-groups/GID/repositories (selected_repository_ids[])
# Private repo ids: gh api orgs/ORG/repos --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.private and (.archived|not)) | .id'
```

Gotcha: the manual run that motivated this task used a temp key file and an EXIT trap that referenced a `local` variable. The trap fired after the function returned, hit `unbound variable` under `set -u`, and left the key on disk. Do not write key material to files. If a file is ever unavoidable, use a global path variable, `chmod 600` before writing, and verify the cleanup.

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh`: the helper described in What. Model it on `github-runner-broker-health-helper.sh`.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md`:
  - Add a section `## Org-scoped GitHub App runners (recommended)` before `## Current deployment`, with the model, a one-time-per-org onboarding checklist and helper usage.
  - Retitle the existing deployment section to show it describes the legacy repo-scoped pool.
  - Add a `runs-on` guidance line: private repos use `[self-hosted, linux, <pool-label>]`; public repos stay on GitHub-hosted runners.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** none at HEAD; this is a new helper. The runbook is the only doc reader (`rg -l github-runner .agents/` lists `reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md` and `workflows/runners-check.md`). `runners-check.md` covers broker health and does not need changes.
- **Writers/mutation paths:**
  - GitHub API: runner-group POST, PATCH and PUT.
  - Remote file write over ssh (`push-key`).
  - No local state files.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-github-runner-broker-health-helper.sh` shows the stubbed-`gh` test pattern if CI policy requires a test for new helpers. Do not add one otherwise.
- **Schemas/config:** none.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` automatically; nothing to register.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Existing manually created groups are reconciled idempotently by `group-ensure`.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR. Runner groups the helper creates can be deleted with `gh api -X DELETE orgs/ORG/actions/runner-groups/GID`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Create the helper skeleton from the broker-health pattern, with explicit `return 0` or `return 1` and `local var="$1"` in every function.
2. Implement `status` first (read-only), then `group-ensure` with `--dry-run`, then `verify-key`, then `push-key`.
3. Key handling:
   - Read the key only from an env var injected by `aidevops secret NAME -- ...`.
   - Never echo the key or the JWT, and never put either in argv.
   - Use `<(...)` or a stdin pipe for openssl and ssh.
   - Print only the public-key SHA-256 (`openssl pkey -pubout | openssl sha256`).
4. `group-ensure` must:
   - Re-read the group after a write and print the effective `visibility`, `allows_public_repositories` and repo list.
   - Exit non-zero if `allows_public_repositories` is true or any selected repo is public.
5. Update the runbook. Use placeholders (`<ORG>`, `<HOST>`, `<POOL_LABEL>`); no real org names, hosts or IPs.
6. Run `shellcheck` on the helper, then `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Two concurrent `group-ensure` runs could both POST, and GitHub rejects the duplicate name. Treat HTTP 409/422 "already exists" as "reconcile existing", not as failure.
- **Migration/rollback:** none. Groups created by hand in the GitHub UI are adopted, not replaced.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** The broker-health helper and the legacy pool runbook text keep working unchanged.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Every command must be safe to re-run. `push-key` overwrites the same path atomically (write to `PATH.tmp` remotely, then `mv`).
- **Partial failure/recovery:** If `push-key` fails part-way, it must leave either the old file or no file, never a partial key. On a fingerprint mismatch, delete the remote temp file.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
.agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh help
# With admin:org gh auth on a test org (read-only and dry-run only, no mutation needed):
.agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh status --org <ORG>
.agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh group-ensure --org <ORG> --name <GROUP> --repos all-private --dry-run
```

- **Surface mapping:**
  - `shellcheck` and lint cover helper style.
  - `status` proves API read handling.
  - `group-ensure --dry-run` proves the plan, the public-repo refusal and the payload, without any write.
  - `verify-key` and `push-key` need a real App key; the maintainer verifies them post-merge (manual criterion).
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:**
- Do not automate GitHub App creation or private-key generation; that needs the GitHub web UI.
- Do not provision server-side runner services; that belongs to the operator's infrastructure repo.
- Never allow public repositories in a runner group.

**AI brief owner:** interactive maintainer session that filed this issue.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-github-runner-org-helper.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The helper exists, passes ShellCheck and exposes `status`, `group-ensure`, `verify-key`, `push-key` and `help`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "shellcheck .agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh && .agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh help | grep -q group-ensure"
  ```

- [ ] `group-ensure` hard-codes `allows_public_repositories=false` and refuses public repos.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "allows_public_repositories=false"
    path: ".agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Key material is never printed or written to local temp files. There is no `mktemp` in the helper's key paths and no echo of the key variable.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: subagent
    prompt: "Review github-runner-org-helper.sh: confirm the App private key and JWT are never printed, placed in argv, or written to local files, and that only the public-key SHA-256 is displayed."
    files: ".agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh"
  ```

- [ ] The runbook documents the org/App/JIT model with placeholders only, and keeps the legacy section.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "## Org-scoped GitHub App runners"
    path: ".agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md"
  ```

- [ ] Post-merge, the maintainer runs `verify-key` and `push-key` against a real org App, and checks that the reported App ID, Installation ID and fingerprints match.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: manual
    prompt: "Run verify-key and push-key against a real org App; confirm IDs and fingerprints match and the remote file is mode 600."
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- One GitHub App per org (only the self-hosted-runners write permission, webhook inactive, installable only on that org). This limits a key compromise to one org. A shared App installed across orgs was ruled out.
- Org-scoped runner groups, restricted to selected private repos. Public repos must never reach self-hosted runners, because fork PRs could run code on the host. Public repos keep free GitHub-hosted minutes.
- Ephemeral JIT registration from App installation tokens is the production server model (one runner per container, own network, rootless Docker per org user). The helper prepares inputs for it and does not reimplement it.
- Key storage: aidevops secret `<ORG>_RUNNERS_APP_KEY` (multiline storage fixed in #34117). Inject one named secret; inject-all `secret run` noise was fixed in #34222.
- Possible follow-up, not in scope: the GitHub App Manifest flow could reduce App creation to one browser confirmation and return the key directly. Verify against GitHub docs before filing.

## Dependencies

- **External:** a `gh` token with `admin:org` for `group-ensure` and `status`; an org GitHub App and its key for `verify-key` and `push-key`; ssh access to the runner host for `push-key`.

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 20m | broker helper skeleton, secret-helper single-secret path, runbook |
| Implementation | 2h | helper (4 subcommands) and runbook section |
| Verification | 20m | shellcheck, lint, help, read-only `status`, `group-ensure --dry-run` |
| **Total** | **~2.7h** | |

<details>

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-10
- **Session:** opencode:issue-first-seed-pr-release-session
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** While releasing v3.38.46, the release lane was stuck on an earlier failed attempt (source PR #34226, `phase=reconcile-required`, `tag=null`, executor dead). The printed hint `aidevops release reconcile 34226` exited 2 (`release-tag-discovery result=not-found`). Re-running the same source, `aidevops release patch 34226 incremental`, recovered the lane and published v3.38.46. The troubleshooting table does not cover this case.

## What

Add one row to the Troubleshooting table in `.agents/workflows/release.md`. It tells operators how to recover a release lane that is `reconcile-required` with no tag, where `reconcile` exits 2.

## Why

The existing row "Another source owns the release lane" says to reconcile the active source. When version-manager failed before tagging, there is no tag to reconcile, `recover-reservation` applies only to the `reserved` phase, and the lane blocks every later release. Without this row the next operator has to read `full-loop-release-helper.sh` and `release-lane-helper.sh` to find the recovery path.

## Tier

`tier:simple`. This is a single exact docs edit; the row text is given below.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/release.md` — in `## Troubleshooting`, insert the row below directly after the row that starts `| Another source owns the release lane |`.

```markdown
| Lane `reconcile-required` with `tag=pending`; `reconcile` exits 2 (tag not found) | Version-manager failed before tagging, so there is nothing to reconcile and `recover-reservation` (reserved phase only) does not apply. Re-run the lane's own source: `aidevops release <type> <lane-source-pr> incremental`. It recovers the failed pre-publication lane, keeps the reviewed authorization, and continues from a fresh pinned snapshot; then follow the normal exit-`8` reconcile flow. |
```

title: full-loop-helper record-published/included-release: misleading and silent errors (--workflow path, missing source receipt)
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release` and `record-included-release` fail without saying why, so a correct release looks like failed or missing evidence.

Observed (aidevops v3.38.45, a non-aidevops plugin repo, release workflow on tag `push`):

1. `record-published-release 432 v1.0.30 <owner/repo> --workflow .github/workflows/release.yml --event push` printed `Cannot record release:published: release, tag, and successful release workflow evidence do not match PR #432`. The evidence did match: the tag, release and successful run were all correct. The real cause was the `--workflow` value. `_full_loop_verify_published_release` only accepts a bare file name or a numeric ID (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\.ya?ml$`), and a path with `/` fails that check with a bare `return 1`. With `--workflow release.yml`, the same command succeeded.
2. `record-included-release <PR> 432 v1.0.30 ...` then exited 1 with **no output at all**. The cause was that the source PR had no `release:published` receipt yet, so a bare `return 1` fired at the receipt checks. Every check in `cmd_record_included_release` before the lock (usage aside) fails silently.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`
  - `_full_loop_parse_published_release_options` (around line 859): validate `--workflow` there and `print_error` a clear message when it is not a bare `*.yml`/`*.yaml` file name or a numeric workflow ID. Optionally accept `.github/workflows/<name>.yml` by taking its basename.
  - `_full_loop_verify_published_release` (around line 763): give each distinct failure its own message on stderr: invalid argument, tag not found or not pointing at the merge commit, release missing or draft, no successful run for the workflow/event/head SHA. The caller's generic "do not match" line is then only a summary.
  - `cmd_record_included_release` (around line 975): replace bare `return 1`s with `print_error` messages, in particular "source PR #N has no release:published receipt; run record-published-release first", and the repository-specific refusal for marcusquinn/aidevops.
- Reference pattern: `cmd_record_no_release` in the same file already prints a reason for every failure.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on the edited file.
- Against any repo with a published tag release: `record-published-release <PR> <TAG> <REPO> --workflow .github/workflows/release.yml --event push` either succeeds or names the invalid `--workflow` value. `record-included-release` run before the source PR's receipt exists names the missing receipt. Every failing path prints one line to stderr.
- `full-loop-helper.sh help` documents the accepted `--workflow` forms.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Circuit-breaker meta: diagnose t2007 cost trip on a private original issue
body:
<!-- aidevops:generator=circuit-breaker-meta-filer -->
<!-- circuit-breaker-meta-original:withheld -->

## What

Diagnose why the **t2007 cost** circuit breaker fired on withheld (private repository) after 4 consecutive worker failure(s), and ship the systemic fix that prevents the same class of failure on subsequent issues.

The breaker tripping is the SYMPTOM. This issue is for finding and fixing the ROOT CAUSE — typically a dispatch path bug, a worker setup race, an exit-classifier defect, or a brief-quality gap that caused workers to crash before reading the brief.

## Why

The existing breaker (`t2007 cost`) halts dispatch with `status:blocked` on the original. Filing this meta-issue converts the trip into a self-healing cycle: forensics → hypothesis → fix → original unblocks automatically.

The original (the private original issue) gets a `blocked-by` label pointing at this meta-issue and clears automatically when this meta-issue's PR merges (handled by `pulse-merge.sh::_unblock_circuit_breaker_meta_pr`).

## Tracking original issue

- Original: withheld (private repository)
- Breaker: `t2007 cost` (`cost-circuit-breaker:fired`)
- Failure count: 4
- Last failure reason: (withheld: private original)
- **Tier**: `tier:standard`
- **Spent**: 952954 tokens
- **Budget**: 800000 tokens

## Hypothesis (starting point — verify first)

The most common root causes for `t2007 cost` trips are:

- **Brief is unimplementable as written** — refine scope or split the task; flag for `needs-decomposition`.
- **Hidden blocker** — missing dependency, environment issue, design conflict that cumulative worker attempts could not resolve.
- **Worker stuck in a loop** — model can't decompose the task; consider tier escalation OR scope reduction.
- **Wrong tier assigned** — downgrade a `tier:thinking` task to `standard`, or vice versa.

title: Scheduled standalone reviews mentioning issues fail the issue-worker environment contract
body:
## Problem

A supported standalone `aidevops schedule once --after 20m --prompt-file <PATH>` review was accepted as queued by an already-loaded scheduler, then failed immediately when due. The review never launched and no result was published. This is a scheduling/runtime contract failure, not a model or application failure.

The bounded prompt was a source/tracker-only completion review that mentioned an issue number in prose; it was not an issue implementation dispatch. Job metadata reported `status: failure`, `attempt: 1`, `duration_seconds: 0`, `outcome: runtime_exit_1`, `error: runtime_failed`. Its complete job log was:

```text
[fatal] WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER unset — issue worker env contract missing; aborting before model launch
```

No project identifiers, private content, credentials, or machine paths are needed to reproduce this.

## Owning source and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/deferred-job-runner.sh:364-372` accepts the prompt dispatch kind with prompt-material validation.
- `.agents/scripts/deferred-job-runner.sh:461-474` invokes the headless helper with `--role worker`; it supplies issue-worktree environment only for that dispatch kind, not standalone prompt jobs.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh:726-737` classifies a worker whose prompt contains `issue #<number>` as an issue worker. Lines 743-805 correctly require issue identity and a matching pre-created worktree for that category.
- `.agents/scripts/deferred-job-helper.sh` documents prompt-file scheduling separately from issue scheduling.

Inspect the existing headless role/capability contracts and deferred-job tests before selecting a repair. Keep strict issue-worker worktree/repository/identity checks intact. Do not synthesize an issue claim, create an implementation worktree, or bypass a safety gate merely to run a report. Use an explicitly supported bounded prompt/report dispatch contract, or reject unsupported combinations at scheduling preflight rather than 20 minutes later. Prose references are not implementation authority.

## Verification

Use existing shell test infrastructure and disposable synthetic prompts only. Cover a standalone report prompt mentioning an issue number, a standalone prompt without that phrase, and a real issue-worktree job. The first two must follow the supported report contract (or fail explicitly before queueing if intentionally unsupported); the issue worker must still fail without its required identity/worktree contract. Prove no model launches during negative tests and preserve exactly-once job accounting. Run affected ShellCheck and existing deferred/headless regression tests; no new scheduler, model calls or production project operations.

## Discovery

Before filing, title search for deferred/prompt found no matching issue; body search for deferred plus WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER returned only old closed pulse-refactor parents, not this standalone-review failure. Source and log evidence were read without running or replaying the failed job. The missed review was completed interactively, not by weakening the runtime guard. Framework repair remains separate from that recovered review.

title: localdev serve misses healthy owned listener readiness
body:
## Goal

Fix `localdev-helper.sh serve` readiness detection when its owned server answers the configured health URL successfully but the helper continues polling until timeout and terminates that server.

## Evidence

Two fresh, foreground, bounded launches used the repository-supported wrappers on an unused loopback port. In both runs:

- the server printed its Next.js ready message;
- an independent `curl` to the exact configured health URL returned the expected HTTP 200 JSON response;
- authenticated API requests also returned HTTP 200;
- the server process belonged to the expected repository tree;
- after 300 seconds, `localdev-helper-serve.sh` printed `Server did not become ready ... within 300s` and terminated the child.

The second run used the verification wrapper, which derives a single loopback origin and skips migrations. Its captured log showed the health response at startup and a rendered authenticated route response before the helper timed out.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-serve.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-localdev-helper-serve.sh`

If the existing test file has a different canonical name, discover the nearest current localdev-helper test and keep the change there.

## Reference pattern

Preserve `_serve_wait_for_readiness`, `_serve_check_existing`, project-root owner validation, health checks, child liveness checks, launch locking, and signal cleanup. Diagnose why `SERVE_EXISTING` remains false despite a healthy owned listener instead of weakening owner or health validation.

## Constraints

- Do not accept foreign listeners or listeners outside the selected project root.
- Do not treat a root-page response as health evidence when a health URL is configured.
- Preserve bounded startup timeout and cleanup of genuinely failed children.
- Keep Bash 3.2 compatibility and explicit function returns.
- Add a regression test that simulates an owned listener becoming healthy after launch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A newly launched, owned listener that returns HTTP 200 from the configured health URL causes `serve` to return readiness instead of timing out.
- [ ] Foreign-owner and unhealthy-listener cases remain rejected.
- [ ] The helper does not terminate a listener after readiness has been established.
- [ ] Existing localdev-helper tests pass.

## Verification

Run the focused localdev-helper shell test suite and a bounded `serve` smoke with a delayed loopback health endpoint.

title: t18645: OpenCode slash commands: stop defaulting hardcoded commands to subtask:true; route per-command by execution model
body:
## Task


OpenCode command files produced by `_maybe_write_hardcoded_command` must stop using `subtask: true` by default. Each hardcoded command needs an explicit, commented decision about whether it runs in the invoking (primary) session or in an OpenCode subtask child, based on its execution model:

- **`/release` → primary session (`subtask` omitted).** `workflows/release.md:31-44` (GH#33488) already requires OpenCode releases to run in the primary session that owns the linked worktree. A child cannot start `aidevops_bounded_operation` in its parent's worktree. The current frontmatter contradicts that.
- **`/onboarding` and `/setup-aidevops`: likely primary.** These are conversational, multi-turn wizards, and a child session returns a single result. Confirm this from the workflow docs before changing them.
- **`/preflight`, `/postflight` and `/agent-review`: decide from evidence.** These are read-mostly and produce a lot of output, so a bounded child can be appropriate. However, if a command must run `aidevops_bounded_operation` in a session-owned worktree or perform git side effects, it belongs in the primary. Record the reason in a generator comment next to each call, following the `review-issue-pr` precedent at lines 722-745.

title: repo_metrics.py: skip-if-fresh uses file mtime, so CI checkouts always skip the metrics refresh
body:
## What

`repo_metrics.py --skip-if-fresh-hours N` decides freshness from the JSON file's modification time (`.agents/scripts/repo_metrics.py`, `outputs_fresh()`: `json_path.stat().st_mtime`). In GitHub Actions the file was just checked out, so its mtime is the checkout time and the outputs always look fresh. The managed Repository metrics workflow (`skip_if_fresh_hours: 24`) therefore never regenerates or commits `docs/metrics/` on push or scheduled runs; only runs without the skip option would.

## Evidence

- wpallstars/seoprostats `docs/metrics/repo-metrics.json` has `"generated_at": "2026-10-06T04:25:48Z"` and was last committed on 2026-10-06.
- Repository metrics runs 38073713877 (2026-10-10 17:55 UTC) and 38074199837 (18:02 UTC) both log `SYNC_PAT present — metrics commit will use PAT`, then `repo metrics fresh: .../docs/metrics/repo-metrics.json`, and commit nothing, although the outputs are four days old.
- The installed framework (3.38.45) still has the `st_mtime` check; the workflow pins v3.38.4 (90993053).

## How

- File: `.agents/scripts/repo_metrics.py`, `outputs_fresh()` (around line 118).
- Read age from the JSON's own `generated_at` (written by the same script, ISO 8601 `Z`); treat a missing or unparsable value as stale. Optionally fall back to the file's last commit time (`git log -1 --format=%ct -- <file>`), never to mtime.
- Keep the required-files check as it is.

## Verification

- In a fresh clone of a repo whose `docs/metrics/repo-metrics.json` has a `generated_at` older than 24h, `python3 .agents/scripts/repo_metrics.py --skip-if-fresh-hours 24 ...` regenerates instead of printing `repo metrics fresh`.
- With a `generated_at` from the last hour it still skips.
- A managed repo's Repository metrics run then logs a `chore(metrics): refresh repository metrics [skip ci]` commit.

body:
## Task


Recognise the sanctioned `blocked-by:GH#NNN` label form everywhere Pulse reads or cleans dependency labels, so an issue whose blocker has closed is automatically unblocked instead of staying `status:blocked` forever.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Recognise the sanctioned `blocked-by:GH#NNN` label form everywhere Pulse reads or cleans dependency labels, so an issue whose blocker has closed is automatically unblocked instead of staying `status:blocked` forever.

## Why (observed evidence)

#34200 (t18639) was created with label `blocked-by:GH#34199`. `claim-task-id.sh` explicitly allows this form (`_BLOCKED_BY_AUTO_CREATE_REGEX='^blocked-by:(t[0-9]+|GH#[0-9]+|#[0-9]+)$'`).
#34199 closed at 2026-10-10T02:31Z. At 06:00Z, after the TODO publication PR merged, `planning-publication-reconcile.sh` `_publication_task_has_dependency` matched `^blocked-by:(GH)?#[1-9][0-9]*$` and applied `status:blocked`, deferring removal to dependency reconciliation. Nothing ever removed it:

- `pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq` (`parsed_issue`, `$label_issue_nums`) and the reference parser in `pulse-dep-graph.sh` (`_dep_graph_process_issue_json`) only accept `^blocked-by:#[0-9]+$`. `GH#34199` is neither a task ID nor a number, so the issue never enters `blocked_by`, and `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` never visits it.
- `_refresh_cleanup_resolved_blocker_labels` only removes `blocked-by:#N`.
- `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` `_der_collect_candidates` searches `label:"blocked-by:#N"` only.

Pulse log evidence: no dep-graph line for #34200 after 06:00Z; the issue stays blocked with a closed blocker.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq` `parsed_issue`: accept `^blocked-by:(GH)?#[0-9]+$` for `$label_issue_nums`, and keep those labels out of the task-ID path.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` `_dep_graph_process_issue_json` (reference parser) to match; `_refresh_cleanup_resolved_blocker_labels` removes both `blocked-by:#N` and `blocked-by:GH#N`.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh` `_der_collect_candidates`: also search `label:"blocked-by:GH#N"`.
- Reference pattern: GH#25922 stale-label cleanup and its test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh
- .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-reduce.sh

## Acceptance

- [ ] An open issue labelled `status:blocked` + `blocked-by:GH#N` with closed #N is unblocked by the graph refresh and the stale label is removed.
- [ ] `blocked-by:GH#N` with open #N keeps the issue blocked.

## Task


Stop a maintainer closing (or reopening) an externally authored, cross-referenced issue from invalidating every signed approval that links to it. Today that state change turns a valid approval into `STALE_APPROVAL` and Pulse blocks dispatch with `ever_nmr_without_approval`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop a maintainer closing (or reopening) an externally authored, cross-referenced issue from invalidating every signed approval that links to it. Today that state change turns a valid approval into `STALE_APPROVAL` and Pulse blocks dispatch with `ever_nmr_without_approval`.

## Why (observed evidence)

- #33629 (external author, `author_association: NONE`) was approved twice with cryptographic signatures (comments 5998563288 and 5998812690, issued 2026-10-05T16:38:03Z).
- The approval snapshot includes a `linked_references` entry for #33633: same external author, cross-referenced at 15:53:32Z, before approval. Its source is `content_bound: true` with `state` included.
- The maintainer closed #33633 as completed at 2026-10-06T05:27:07Z.
- `approval-helper.sh verify issue 33629 marcusquinn/aidevops` now returns `STALE_APPROVAL` (`APPROVAL_REASON: stale-or-unproven-continuity`). An xtrace showed `_approval_verify_locked_issue_continuity` fails at `_approval_continuity_content_changes` because the title and body digests match but the **frame** digest differs. The only frame drift found in a current-snapshot dump is the linked source `state: closed`. Lifecycle labels are replaced by the signed lifecycle, and the post-approval comments are maintainer-authored.
- Pulse logs `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=permission_grant_unverified signal=STALE_APPROVAL` and `ever_nmr_without_approval` for #33629.

## How

Trust-boundary change: mark it `#aidevops:trust-boundary` and keep it fail-closed.

- `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` `_approval_snapshot_v2_linked_source_content` (around line 182): for untrusted, content-bound sources, keep binding `title` and `body` but stop treating `state` as scope-bearing. As an alternative, accept a state change in continuity only when a timeline `closed`/`reopened` event shows a write-authorized actor. Pick one and record why in the PR.
- Mirror the change in `source_access_core._issue_reference`, which the comment at line 181 names as its twin.
- Existing approvals carry the old digest. Either add a profile fallback in `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh` `_approval_classify_digest_mismatch`, following the STABLE/LEGACY profile pattern, or document that affected issues need a fresh signature.

- .agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh
- .agents/scripts/source_access_core.py
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh

- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` passes, with the new cases included; ShellCheck is clean.

title: sync-workflows: commented example uses: line is read and rewritten as the live caller ref
body:
## Problem

`sync-workflows-helper.sh` treats a commented example `uses:` line as the live caller line.

The current `loc-badge-caller.yml` template contains an example inside a comment, before the real `uses:` line:

```yaml
    #   uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml@<40-char-sha> # vX.Y.Z
    #   aidevops_ref: <40-char-sha> # vX.Y.Z
    uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml@main
```

Observed effects:

1. `_extract_ref_pin` (`grep ... | head -1`) returns `@<40-char-sha>` for a caller rendered from the current template. Dry run on a downstream repo planned `update runner → .github/workflows/loc-badge.yml at ref @<40-char-sha>`. Applying it would write the placeholder into the executable `uses:` line, which breaks the workflow.
2. The first sed expression in `_render_template_with_target` rewrites the `@ref` on the commented example as well. A downstream refresh produced `#   uses: ...loc-badge-reusable.yml@d839839... # vX.Y.Z` while the next comment line still says `aidevops_ref: <40-char-sha>`, so the example became inconsistent.

## Fix

- `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` `_extract_ref_pin`: match only non-comment lines (`^[[:space:]]*uses:`).
- `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` `_render_template_with_target`: anchor the `uses:` ref rewrite to the start of the line (with optional indentation) so commented examples are left alone.
- Check `check-workflows-helper.sh` and any other `uses:` ref extraction for the same pattern.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh`
- Dry run `sync-workflows-helper.sh --repo <owner/repo> --workflow loc-badge` on a repo whose caller was rendered from the current template reports the real `@main`/SHA ref, not `@<40-char-sha>`.
- Render the loc-badge template with a SHA ref and confirm the commented example still contains `<40-char-sha>`.

title: fix: init and badges sync add loc-badge.yml beside an existing metrics caller
body:
## Problem

`aidevops init` (`.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh`, repo metrics block near `_wf_dest=".../loc-badge.yml"`) and `badges-sync-helper.sh` (`_install_workflow`) install `.github/workflows/loc-badge.yml` whenever that file name is missing. A repository that already calls `marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml` from another workflow (for example a WordPress starter's pinned `repo-metrics.yml`) gets a second, unpinned `@main` caller: two metrics jobs on every push, racing to commit `docs/metrics/`.

Observed in a managed private plugin repository: `repo-metrics.yml` (pinned v3.38.4) and `loc-badge.yml` (`@main`) both present; the duplicate was removed by hand.

## Reproducer

1. In a test repository with a remote, add `.github/workflows/repo-metrics.yml` whose job has `uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml@<sha>`.
2. Run `badges-sync-helper.sh` in dry-run mode for that repository (or `aidevops init`).
3. Observed: it plans/installs `.github/workflows/loc-badge.yml` ("install → .github/workflows/loc-badge.yml"). Expected: skipped, because a metrics caller already exists.

Source evidence: `_install_workflow` in `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh` checks only `[[ -f "$_path/.github/workflows/loc-badge.yml" ]]`; `aidevops-init-lib.sh` checks only `! -f "$_wf_dest"`.

## Change

Before installing, skip when any file in `.github/workflows/` already references `loc-badge-reusable.yml` in a non-comment `uses:` line (reuse the commented-example-aware parsing from GH#34269 in `sync-workflows-helper.sh` / `check-workflows-helper.sh`). Report it as skipped ("metrics caller already present: <file>").

Files: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh`, `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`; possibly a shared detector in an existing lib. Tests: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-loc-badge-reusable-install.sh` if it covers install decisions.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-loc-badge-reusable-install.sh`

## Verification

- A fixture repo with `.github/workflows/repo-metrics.yml` calling `loc-badge-reusable.yml`: `badges-sync-helper.sh` (dry run) reports skipped; `aidevops init` creates no `loc-badge.yml`.
- A repo with only a commented example `# uses: .../loc-badge-reusable.yml@...` still gets `loc-badge.yml`.

title: docs: self-hosted runners guide covers CI_RUNNER variable and Free-plan org variables
body:
## Problem

`.agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md` says private repos use `[self-hosted, linux, <POOL_LABEL>]` and public repos stay GitHub-hosted, but not how one shared/template workflow serves both. Observed while onboarding an org's private repos: an organization variable `CI_RUNNER` shared with selected private repos was listed by `repos/<ORG>/<REPO>/actions/organization-variables`, yet the workflow saw it empty (GitHub Free plan) and the job fell back to `ubuntu-latest`. title: t18649: Docker cleanup: owner labels, post-merge teardown and pulse reaping for disposable test stacks
body:
## Task


Give aidevops ownership and cleanup for the Docker resources that sessions and scripts create (disposable WordPress/app test sites, plugin-check stacks, review/verification sites), so they are removed once the work that needed them is finished:

1. **Owner labels.** A new `docker-resource-helper.sh` prints the `--label` arguments (and a Compose `labels:` snippet) that mark a container, network or volume as aidevops-owned: `sh.aidevops.owner=1`, `sh.aidevops.repo=<owner/repo>`, `sh.aidevops.ref=<GH#N or PR#N>`, `sh.aidevops.worktree=<path>`, `sh.aidevops.created=<epoch>`, `sh.aidevops.ttl-hours=<N>` (default 72). Docs and framework scripts that start disposable stacks use it.
2. **Teardown after merge.** When the post-merge cleanup removes a linked worktree, it also removes the labelled containers, networks and volumes whose `sh.aidevops.worktree` matches it.
3. **Regular cleanup.** A pulse step removes labelled resources whose worktree is gone and whose linked issue/PR is closed/merged, or whose TTL has expired. It runs report-only until `AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_REAP=1` (default 0 for the first release). Resources without `sh.aidevops.owner=1` are never removed by the pulse; they are only counted in the report.
4. **Pressure report.** `docker-resource-helper.sh report` prints counts and sizes of unused volumes, images and build cache, networks with no containers, and containers stopped longer than the TTL, with the safe commands to reclaim each. It deletes nothing.
5. **Address-pool guidance.** Document the `all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted` error: find networks with no containers, remove only those, and optionally set Docker's `default-address-pools` (for example `{"base":"10.200.0.0/16","size":24}`) for about 256 networks instead of about 30.

## Done when

- [ ] `docker-resource-helper.sh labels` prints the six `sh.aidevops.*` labels; a stack started with them appears in `inventory`.
- [ ] After `full-loop-helper.sh merge` removes a worktree, labelled resources for that worktree are gone (containers, network, volume).
- [ ] `reap` without `--apply`, and the pulse step with `AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_REAP` unset, remove nothing and list candidates.
- [ ] Negative: an unlabelled container/network/volume is never removed by `reap --apply` or the pulse, only counted in `report`.
- [ ] Negative: a labelled resource whose worktree still exists, or whose ref is open, or whose ref lookup failed, is not removed before its TTL; a running one is never removed by the TTL rule.
- [ ] With `docker` missing or the daemon stopped, pulse cleanup and post-merge cleanup still exit 0 with no extra delay beyond the short timeout.
- [ ] `tools/containers/disposable-resources.md` documents the labelled start, teardown, report and the address-pool fix, and is linked from `reference/domain-index.md`.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/docker-resource-helper.sh` — subcommands `labels`, `compose-labels`, `inventory`, `teardown --worktree <path>`, `reap [--apply] [--max-seconds N]`, `report`. Model the dry-run/`--force` split and logging on `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:1174-1179` — in `cleanup_stale_opencode`, after the `system-cleanup.sh` call, run `docker-resource-helper.sh reap --max-seconds "${PULSE_DOCKER_CLEANUP_MAX_SECONDS:-30}"` (plus `--apply` only when `AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_REAP=1`), output to `$LOGFILE`, non-fatal (`|| true`). Same `-x` guard as the `system-cleanup.sh` block. Do **not** hook into `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`: it is 2,024 lines, already over the 1,500-line shell file-size gate.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh:494-500` — after `_merge_remove_worktree_for_cleanup` succeeds, run `docker-resource-helper.sh teardown --worktree "$worktree_path"` non-fatally (`|| true`), only when `docker` is on PATH and the daemon answers.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh:997` — add the owner labels to the plugin-check network, volume and containers it creates (keep `wprh_pc_cleanup`).
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-docker-resource-helper.sh` — PATH-stubbed `docker` (no real daemon) covering the acceptance criteria.
- `NEW: .agents/tools/containers/disposable-resources.md` — how to start a labelled disposable site (`docker run`/Compose examples using the helper), teardown, the report, and the address-pool fix.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/containers/orbstack.md` — one Troubleshooting line pointing to the new doc for the address-pool error and cleanup.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/domain-index.md:67` — add `tools/containers/disposable-resources.md` to the Infrastructure row.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/docker-resource-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-docker-resource-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/containers/disposable-resources.md`
- `.agents/tools/containers/orbstack.md`
- `.agents/reference/domain-index.md`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-integration.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh`

**Integration scope recovery (worker, GH#34285):** `_merge_cleanup_linked_worktree` in `full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh` has no callers on the default branch (`rg -n _merge_cleanup_linked_worktree .agents/scripts` returns only its definition); `cmd_merge` always records a deferred cleanup receipt, and the linked worktree is removed later through `worktree-helper.sh remove` (`_remove_cleanup_and_execute` -> `_remove_finalize_post_removal` in `worktree-helper-cmds.sh`, which already frees localdev/preview resources from `worktree-helper-integration.sh`). The post-merge Docker teardown therefore lives in that shared post-removal hook (a guarded `docker_resource_auto_teardown` beside `preview_proxy_auto_free`), covering merge cleanup and manual removal; the pulse's post-merge removal runs `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` (`pulse-cleanup-worktree-state.sh`), whose removal path in `worktree-clean-lib.sh` (beside `localdev_auto_branch_rm`) gets the same one-line guarded call. Code file size is not gated (`linters-local.sh`: only Markdown size is ratcheted). `full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh` is left unchanged because its helper already routes through `worktree-helper.sh remove`. Collision check: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open related PRs.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** pulse preflight `cleanup_stale_opencode` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:1161`; post-merge `_merge_cleanup_linked_worktree` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh:475`; plugin-check stack in `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh:926-1070`; agents reading `tools/containers/*.md` via `.agents/reference/domain-index.md:67`. Search evidence: `rg -n -i docker` over `system-cleanup.sh`, `pulse-cleanup.sh`, `pulse-cleanup-fixture-orphans.sh`, `full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh` returns nothing today.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `docker rm -f`, `docker network rm`, `docker volume rm`, only through `docker-resource-helper.sh` and only on resources carrying `sh.aidevops.owner=1`. Existing writer kept as-is: `wprh_pc_cleanup` (`wp-plugin-release-helper.sh:932-936`).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh` (merge cleanup), `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh` (pulse stage list, includes `cleanup_stale_opencode`). New `.agents/scripts/tests/test-docker-resource-helper.sh` with a PATH-stubbed `docker` is justified because the reap rule deletes data and a stub is the cheapest way to prove the negative cases without a daemon.
- **Schemas/config:** label keys are the schema; env `AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_REAP` (default 0), `AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_TTL_HOURS` (default 72), `PULSE_DOCKER_CLEANUP_MAX_SECONDS` (default 30). No `configs/*.json` change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh --non-interactive` deploys `.agents/scripts/` and `.agents/tools/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/`; no generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A — no stored state; existing unlabelled resources are never labelled retroactively and are only reported. Evidence: the labels are new, so nothing reads them before this change.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; labels already on resources are inert without the helper. Leaving `AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_REAP` unset (default) disables removal by the pulse without a revert; post-merge teardown can be disabled with `AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_TEARDOWN=0`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Write `docker-resource-helper.sh` with `labels`/`compose-labels` first, then `inventory` (labelled resources as TSV: kind, id, name, repo, ref, worktree, created, ttl, state), `report`, `teardown`, `reap`.
2. Ownership rule for `reap`: remove a labelled resource only if (a) its `sh.aidevops.worktree` path no longer exists **and** its `sh.aidevops.ref` issue/PR is closed/merged, or (b) `now - created > ttl-hours` and it has no running container. Remove containers before networks and volumes; skip a network or volume still attached to any container not being removed.
3. Bound GitHub lookups: one `gh` call per distinct ref per cycle, cached for the cycle; on API failure, skip (never treat unknown as closed).
4. Add the pulse call in `cleanup_stale_opencode`; report-only unless `AIDEVOPS_DOCKER_REAP=1`.
5. Add teardown to post-merge cleanup.
6. Label the plugin-check stack in `wp-plugin-release-helper.sh`.
7. Write the doc, the orbstack line and the index entry.
8. WIP commit, then run verification.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** another session may be starting or using a stack. Never reap a resource created in the last 30 minutes; re-check running state and the worktree path immediately before each removal; a pulse run and a post-merge teardown racing on the same object both tolerate "No such container/network/volume".
- **Migration/rollback:** no data migration. Ordering inside a removal: containers first, then networks, then volumes; skip a network or volume still attached to any container that is not being removed. Rollback is a PR revert; removed volumes are not recoverable, which is why reaping is report-only by default.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older checkouts and ad-hoc commands don't add labels; their resources stay unmanaged (reported only), exactly as today. Docker without label support is not a concern (labels exist since Docker 1.6).
- **Idempotency/retry:** removing an already-removed object is ignored; repeated runs converge. A failed `gh` ref lookup means "keep" for this cycle, retried next cycle.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if removal stops part-way (timeout, daemon restart), the next run re-inventories from labels and finishes; no local state file to corrupt. Docker missing or the daemon down: every entry point returns 0 with one log line, using a short `docker info` timeout, so pulse and merge never fail or slow because of Docker.
- **Data loss:** volumes may hold a test site someone still wants. Mitigations: owner label required, worktree-gone **and** ref-closed (or TTL with nothing running), report-only default, `inventory` shows exactly what would go.
- **Portability and budget:** follow `reference/bash-compat.md` (Bash 3.2: no `mapfile`, no GNU-only `date`); honour `--max-seconds` like `system-cleanup.sh`.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-docker-resource-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh
.agents/scripts/docker-resource-helper.sh report
```

- **Surface mapping:** `linters-local.sh --changed` → ShellCheck and markdown lint for every file in Files Scope (style, `local var="$1"`, explicit returns). `test-docker-resource-helper.sh` → `docker-resource-helper.sh` ownership rule, report-only default, unlabelled/open-ref/lookup-failure negatives, daemon-down exit 0 (acceptance criteria 1, 3, 4, 5, 6; Concurrency and Partial-failure hazards). `test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh` → `full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh` still removes worktrees with Docker absent (criteria 2, 6). `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh` → `pulse-cleanup.sh` still exposes the `cleanup_stale_opencode` stage the pulse schedules (criterion 6). `docker-resource-helper.sh report` on a machine with Docker → real inventory, no deletions (criterion 3).
- **Manual check (machine with Docker):** start a labelled container + network + volume with a temporary worktree path, delete the path, close-state stub or TTL 0, run `reap` (lists it) then `reap --apply` (removes it); an unlabelled container beside it is untouched.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure changes.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

WIP commit after step 7, before running the broader checks.

### Safety-Stop Recovery

If removal logic cannot be made safe within the PR, ship labels, `inventory`, `report`, `teardown` and docs with reaping left report-only, keep this issue open, and record the remaining reaping criteria in a comment.

title: record-published-release misses tag-push release runs unless --event push is given
body:
## Observed

In a maintained non-aidevops repo whose release workflow runs on a `push` of a `vX.Y.Z` tag (`on: push: tags:`), after a verified merge and a successful tag-push release run whose `head_sha` equals the merge SHA:

```
full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release <PR> vX.Y.Z <owner/repo> --workflow release.yml
[ERROR] No successful release run of workflow release.yml found for <merge_sha>
[ERROR] Cannot record release:published: release, tag, and successful release workflow evidence do not match PR #<PR>
```

Adding `--event push` recorded it at once:

```
full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release <PR> vX.Y.Z <owner/repo> --workflow release.yml --event push
[SUCCESS] release:published recorded for merged PR #<PR> (tag=vX.Y.Z)
```

The run's API record: `event: push`, `head_branch: vX.Y.Z`, `conclusion: success`, `path: .github/workflows/release.yml`.

## Change

Either default `record-published-release` to look for runs of the named workflow with `head_branch == TAG` across `push` and `release`/`workflow_dispatch` events (keeping the exact `head_sha` check), or, when no run is found for the default event, say in the error which events exist for that SHA and suggest `--event push`.

Files: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` (the `record-published-release` path and its helper library, found with `rg -n "record-published-release|No successful release run" .agents/scripts`), and the Manual releases paragraph of `.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md` / `workflows/release.md` if the default changes.

## Verification

In a repo with a tag-push release workflow, `record-published-release PR TAG REPO --workflow release.yml` without `--event` records `release:published` (or prints the `--event push` hint), and a mismatched SHA still fails.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`

Implementation: retain the release-event default and add exact-workflow, exact-SHA event diagnostics on missing release runs; suggest --event push only for a successful matching tag-push run. Verification: ShellCheck and the existing completion-evidence suite, including mismatched-SHA rejection.

title: t18650: fix(pulse): async housekeeping still dies before preflight_ownership_reconcile, starving parent/merged-PR reconcile
body:
## Task


Async post-dispatch housekeeping still dies before its last stage, `preflight_ownership_reconcile`, in about a third of runs. That stage runs `reconcile_issues_single_pass`, which closes completed parent-task trackers, merged-PR issues and stale `status:done` issues. Those reconciles are therefore starved for whole cycles, even after GH#33256.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Async post-dispatch housekeeping still dies before its last stage, `preflight_ownership_reconcile`, in about a third of runs. That stage runs `reconcile_issues_single_pass`, which closes completed parent-task trackers, merged-PR issues and stale `status:done` issues. Those reconciles are therefore starved for whole cycles, even after GH#33256.

## Evidence (local pulse.log, 2026-10-10, ~130k lines)

- `Async post-dispatch housekeeping: started` = 66, `... complete` = 43, `... reclaiming stale lock` = 23. `_pulse_acquire_post_dispatch_housekeeping_lock` reclaims only when `kill -0 <pid>` fails, so 23 runs died. They were not displaced while alive.
- Stage order in `_pulse_run_post_dispatch_housekeeping_stages` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`): coderabbit_review → post_merge_scanner → auto_decomposer_scanner (257s observed) → dedup_cleanup → fast_fail_prune_expired → `_pulse_run_blocker_refresh_catchup` (build_dependency_graph_cache 482s + refresh_blocked_status_from_graph 128s + release_repaired_brief_holds 407s observed) → `preflight_ownership_reconcile` (598s observed).
- The run that started at log line 127226 reached `release_repaired_brief_holds` (128131) and then disappeared. The next cycle logged `reclaiming stale lock (pid=49956)` (128643). The new run then restarted at blocker catch-up. `preflight_ownership_reconcile` last ran at line 126078, so its starvation spanned several cycles.
- Concrete impact: after GH#34281 (PRs #34282/#34284) was deployed, external parents #34180/#34125 waited for a housekeeping run that survived long enough to reach reconcile.

## Root cause (confirmed)

Setup reconciliation kills the housekeeping on every deploy. `setup.sh` runs from `auto-update` after each new main commit and from interactive deploys. It calls `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` `_stop_reconciliation_processes`, which SIGTERMs every Pulse runtime process. The detached housekeeping subshell's argv is `bash pulse-wrapper.sh`, so it matches `_PULSE_PATTERN` whatever its process group. GH#33256's `set -m` only protects it from process-group teardown.

- 19 of 24 dead housekeeping PIDs in pulse.log appear in `Stopping pre-reconciliation Pulse process(es): ...` lists in `~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log` / `pulse-wrapper.log` (for example 32467 and 49038). The other 5 coincide with interactive `setup.sh --non-interactive` deploys, whose output is not written to those logs.
- launchd shows the pulse job's last exit as `-15` (SIGTERM). With no TERM trap the wrapper's EXIT trap never runs, which also explains the repeated `Stale mkdir lock detected (owner PID … is dead)` lines in pulse-wrapper.log.
- Stopping old-bundle processes on deploy is intended, because new code must replace old code. The defect is that housekeeping takes 30+ minutes and always restarts from its first stage. On a busy day with many deploys, its last stage (`preflight_ownership_reconcile`) is starved indefinitely.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh

## Fix direction

1. Persist per-stage completion (for example, a small state file next to the housekeeping lock with `stage=epoch` lines, written after each stage finishes). A run that reclaims a stale lock should skip stages completed within a freshness window (for example, < 30 min) and resume at the first incomplete stage. A clean, complete run clears or refreshes the state.
2. Move `preflight_ownership_reconcile` ahead of `_pulse_run_blocker_refresh_catchup`, so the cheap terminal reconciles (parent close, merged-PR close) are not queued behind roughly 17 minutes of graph rebuild and brief-hold release.
3. Add a TERM/HUP trap in the housekeeping subshell that logs `Async post-dispatch housekeeping: terminated by <signal> during <stage>` before exiting, so future deaths are attributable from pulse.log alone.
4. Do not exempt housekeeping from setup reconciliation; old-bundle code must still be replaced on deploy. Keep stage timeouts and the GH#33246 catch-up semantics intact.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh` (extend it to cover the stage-order/resume contract).
- `shellcheck -x` on modified files.
- Runtime: after deploy, the ratio of `Async post-dispatch housekeeping: complete` to `started` in pulse.log approaches 1. `Stage start: preflight_ownership_reconcile` appears in every housekeeping run that survives past the scanners.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

title: t18651: fix(pulse): reconcile single pass starts parent-close mutations it cannot finish before the 380s stage kill
body:
## Task


`reconcile_issues_single_pass` checks its 360s budget (`RECONCILE_TIME_BUDGET_SECS`) only between issues. The outer `run_stage_with_timeout` kill fires at 380s (`_preflight_ownership_reconcile` caps the stage at 380s). A multi-round-trip mutation that starts near the budget (a parent-task close does trust, child and snapshot-stability re-reads, then `gh issue close`, a post-close stability check, an optional compensating reopen and a comment) can therefore be SIGKILLed mid-action. The close then lands without its postcondition/compensation step or log line.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`reconcile_issues_single_pass` checks its 360s budget (`RECONCILE_TIME_BUDGET_SECS`) only between issues. The outer `run_stage_with_timeout` kill fires at 380s (`_preflight_ownership_reconcile` caps the stage at 380s). A multi-round-trip mutation that starts near the budget (a parent-task close does trust, child and snapshot-stability re-reads, then `gh issue close`, a post-close stability check, an optional compensating reopen and a comment) can therefore be SIGKILLed mid-action. The close then lands without its postcondition/compensation step or log line.

## Evidence (local pulse.log, 2026-10-10)

- Line 131190: `Stage start: reconcile_issues_single_pass (timeout 380s)`. Line 131425: `Stage timeout: reconcile_issues_single_pass exceeded 380s (pid 82095)` at 22:38:00Z.
- Parent #34180 was closed at 22:36:34Z, and its close comment was posted at 22:37:11Z. The `Reconcile parent-task: closed #34180 … trust=…` line from `pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh` (after `gh_issue_comment`) never reached any log, so the kill landed inside the close action.
- Earlier timeout at line 126161. Most other runs end via the inner `time-budget abort at 36Xs`, which shows the pass runs at its budget ceiling every cycle.

## Root cause

The per-issue gate in `_pir_reconcile_issue_rows` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`) only stops starting new issues. Nothing checks the remaining time before beginning a multi-call mutation, and the 20s gap between the inner budget (360s) and the outer kill (380s) is smaller than one parent close.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh

## Fix direction

1. Add a small helper (for example `_pir_budget_allows_mutation <min_seconds>`) that uses the existing `_t2984_start_ts`/`_t2984_budget` locals (dynamic scope) and returns 1 when the remaining budget is below a mutation reserve (for example 90s for parent close, configurable).
2. Call it at the start of the parent-close path, before the first live re-read, and in any other multi-step close/reopen action. When the budget is short, skip the issue for this cycle with a log line (`deferred: insufficient reconcile budget for parent close`) instead of starting.
3. Do not raise the outer 380s cap or the 360s budget. Keep stage-4 trust/close gates unchanged.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`: add a case where the budget is nearly exhausted and assert that the parent close is deferred (no `gh issue close` call) and logged.
- `shellcheck -x` on modified files.
- Runtime: no `Stage timeout: reconcile_issues_single_pass` lines that follow a `gh issue close` without the matching `Reconcile parent-task: closed` log line.

</details>

title: docs: repo setup guidance says to keep Qlty and skip its out-of-minutes check on organisation repos
body:
## What

Repository setup and management guidance should say what `reference/ci-gate-policy.md` rule 14 already enforces at merge time. On organisation repositories, public or private, Qlty's GitHub App has a monthly minutes allowance. When it runs out, the "qlty check" fails with "Qlty did not run because you are out of minutes". The merge paths already skip that (`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` `apply_qlty_billing_policy`, `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` `_pmrc_repo_has_qlty_credit_limit`).

The setup docs agents read when adding or managing repos don't say so. In one owner session, an agent took a red qlty check as a reason to remove Qlty from an organisation. It edited docs in four repositories and asked the owner to uninstall the app, when the intended policy is to keep it for the free minutes and skip the out-of-minutes check.

## Changes

- `.agents/tools/code-review/qlty.md`: Quick Reference bullet and a "GitHub App: monthly minutes" section. Keep the app installed; an out-of-minutes failure is billing, not a reason to uninstall, rerun, change code or file issues; never make "qlty check" a required status check on a credit-limited repository; real findings still count.
- `.agents/tools/code-review/setup.md`: Qlty in the platform table and a troubleshooting row for "out of minutes".
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-new.md`: an out-of-minutes qlty check still proves the app is connected; skip it per rule 14.

## Verification

- `rg -n 'rule 14' .agents/tools/code-review/qlty.md .agents/tools/code-review/setup.md .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-new.md` finds each pointer.
- markdownlint on the changed files.
