body:
**Task ID:** `t18662` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): release dependency-ready issues held only by brief terminal-blocker text

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `dependency event reconciler terminal blocker vocabulary body hold false positive` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found 0 open related PRs for the target files; last relevant changes are 0e83416a58 (t18661 supersession readiness), 589016c402 (t18646 blocked-by:GH# labels), 74f9d071c8 (GH#33957 resumable stale sweep), 2227f6fcf7 (GH#33881 blocked-by value grammar)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main c30e0ba4fd: `_der_text_has_strong_hold`, `_der_has_hold`, `_der_try_unblock`, `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` (`.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`); runtime terminal-blocker writers `_apply_terminal_blocker` (`pulse-dispatch-core.sh`) and `_terminal_blocker_recovery` / `terminal_blocker_circuit_comment` (`terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`) post comments only
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — narrow change on the unblock safety path; every new branch keeps or adds a hold, except the documented body-vocabulary exemption
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found while maximising worker throughput for a managed private repo's enrichment backlog: issues whose dependencies had all closed stayed `status:blocked` indefinitely.

## What

The dependency-event reconciler (close events and the periodic stale sweep) releases `status:blocked` issues whose dependencies are resolved, without treating worker-protocol documentation in the issue body as a hold, and without overriding blocks that no dependency explains:

1. Terminal-blocker vocabulary (`Terminal[_ -]blocker`, which also matches `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=` and `terminal-blocker circuit`) is hold evidence only in trusted comments, not in the issue body. Every other strong marker, operational hold line and hold label keeps its current scope.
2. The reconciler only removes `status:blocked` with positive dependency evidence: at least one native `blockedBy` edge, or a declared blocker ref in the body or a `blocked-by:` label. Without either, the block came from another mechanism and is left alone.
3. A close event keeps reconciling the remaining dependants when one dependant is still waiting on another open blocker (`DER_NOT_READY`), instead of stopping at it. Hard failures still stop the pass.

## Why

`_der_has_hold` runs `_der_text_has_strong_hold` over `body + trusted comments`, and its pattern includes `Terminal[_ -]blocker([_ -]detected)?`. Briefs routinely document the worker protocol in the body, for example: "On exit 1 ... emit `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`. Do not set `status:blocked`: the terminal-blocker circuit keeps this issue `status:available`". The runtime never records terminal-blocker state in bodies — `_apply_terminal_blocker` and the terminal-blocker circuit post comments — so in a body this vocabulary is documentation, not a hold. The dep-graph refresh body gate (`issue_body_has_defer_marker`) already ignores it.

Read-only census of one managed private repo (2026-10-11, 340 open `status:blocked` issues):

- 237 bodies (70%) contain terminal-blocker vocabulary; no other strong hold token appears in any body.
- 11 issues with every dependency closed (10 native, 1 declared) had the body text as their only hold signal, so neither close events nor the stale sweep could release them.
- 3 issues with no dependency at all were blocked by mechanisms the reconciler does not recognise (two cost-circuit-breaker trips, one dispatch infrastructure failure). Only the body text stopped the reconciler from releasing them, because with no native edge and no declared ref `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed` is vacuously true. Change 1 alone would release them, so change 2 is required. It also matches the existing contract in `_hold_dependency_sync_retry` (`issue-sync-relationships-gh.sh`): "Pulse supplies the positive proof required to unblock it".

Change 3 is a code-level defect present since GH#27338: in `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure`, `_der_try_unblock ... || return 1` treats `DER_NOT_READY` (the dependant has another open blocker) as fatal. All later dependants of the closed issue then wait for the stale sweep instead of being released by the close event.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
  - Split the strong-hold pattern into `DER_STRONG_HOLD_RE` (`HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED|Worker Watchdog Kill|ACTION REQUIRED|worker[_ -]blocked|aidevops:brief-hold`) and `DER_TERMINAL_BLOCKER_RE` (`Terminal[_ -]blocker([_ -]detected)?`).
  - `_der_text_has_strong_hold <text> <comments>`: `DER_STRONG_HOLD_RE` over `<text>` (body + comments, unchanged scope), `DER_TERMINAL_BLOCKER_RE` over `<comments>` only, and the existing `**BLOCKED**` + `cannot proceed` pair over `<text>`.
  - `_der_has_hold`: pass `"$text" "$comments"`; the expired-brief-hold rewrite still applies to `comments` first.
  - New `_der_declares_blockers <candidate_json>`: true when `_der_issue_refs` or `_der_task_refs` yields a ref from body + label names (same text construction as `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed`); jq failure is false.
  - `_der_try_unblock`: when `_DER_NATIVE_BLOCKERS_PRESENT` is not `true`, `_der_declares_blockers "$candidate_json" || return 0` before `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed`.
  - `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure`: capture the `_der_try_unblock` status per candidate; continue on `0` or `DER_NOT_READY`, `return 1` otherwise.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh` — classifier cases for body vs comment terminal-blocker vocabulary; stale-sweep cases for body-documented protocol (released) and a no-evidence block (kept); a two-dependant close event where the first is still blocked and the second is released. Add fixture knobs `STALE_DEP_LABEL` (stale-sweep dependency label, default `blocked-by:#10`), `EXTRA_DEPENDANT` (second search candidate #21) and `NATIVE_EXTRA_FOR` (restrict the extra open native blocker to one issue number).

### Complexity Impact

- `_der_text_has_strong_hold` 10 → ~13 lines; `_der_try_unblock` 24 → ~26; `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` 32 → ~35; new helper ~10 lines. All far below the 100-line gate; file ~720 lines.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_der_try_unblock` from `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` (close hooks in `pulse-merge.sh`, `full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, `issue-sync-helper-close.sh`, `github-cli-helper.sh`) and `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`). `_der_completion_blockers_closed` does not use the hold classifier and is unchanged.
- **Deliberately unchanged:** dep-graph refresh (`pulse-dep-graph.sh`) only visits issues with dependency entries and already ignores body terminal-blocker text; dispatch-time `terminal_blocker_circuit_active` / `terminal_blocker_backoff_active` remain the authority for re-dispatch after a worker BLOCKED exit.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** no new writes; the only label edit is the existing re-read-guarded `status:blocked` → `status:available` in `_der_try_unblock`.
- **Schemas/config:** none.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none; the next stale sweep applies the rule to existing issues.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; no persisted state.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Safety direction:** change 1 can only release issues whose dependencies are positively resolved and that carry no comment, label or operational hold; changes 2 and 3 never release anything new on their own (2 adds a hold, 3 continues to the same per-candidate checks).
- **Comment-side vocabulary unchanged:** trusted terminal-blocker comments (observations, circuit comments, `Terminal blocker detected`) still hold, including after this change.
- **Evidence removed after blocking:** an issue whose only dependency declaration was deleted stays `status:blocked` until a maintainer or the owning mechanism releases it — the conservative outcome the dependency-sync retry hold already relies on.
- **Mixed versions:** older runners keep the old classifier; both only ever release fully resolved dependants.
- **Partial failure:** API/jq failures keep returning 1 (fail closed); `DER_NOT_READY` is no longer escalated to a failure in the close-event loop.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-supersession-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-closing-reconciliation.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Runtime:** after deployment, the next stale sweep of the census repo releases the dependency-resolved issues whose only hold was body text (stale-sweep log line plus label timeline), while the no-dependency cost-breaker and infrastructure-failure blocks stay `status:blocked`.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18662-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_der_has_hold` returns no hold for a body containing only terminal-blocker worker-protocol text, and still returns a hold for the same vocabulary in a trusted comment, for `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED` / `ACTION REQUIRED` in the body, and for every existing classifier case.
- [ ] The stale sweep releases a `status:blocked` issue whose dependencies are closed and whose body documents the terminal-blocker protocol.
- [ ] The stale sweep leaves a `status:blocked` issue with no native edge, no declared ref and no `blocked-by:` label unchanged, even with no hold markers.
- [ ] A close event with two dependants, where the first still has another open blocker, releases the second.
- [ ] Existing reconciler, supersession and stale-recovery suites pass; ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed` are clean.

## Context & Decisions

- Only the terminal-blocker family moves to comment scope: it is the only strong token observed in bodies, and every runtime writer of it posts comments. `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED`, `ACTION REQUIRED`, `aidevops:brief-hold`, watchdog and `worker_blocked` markers keep body scope; the existing "strong machine markers remain authoritative inside examples" decision stands.
- Not in scope: relaxing comment-side terminal-blocker holds (the dispatch-time circuit already decides retries, but trusted comments stay holds here), teaching the reconciler cost-breaker or infrastructure-failure markers (the evidence guard leaves those blocks to their own release paths), and dep-graph refresh budget or starvation.
- A worker BLOCKED release without an observation comment (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` alone) is not a reconciler hold today and stays that way; the dispatch-time backoff and circuit handle repeated blocked releases.

</details>

body:
**Task ID:** `t18663` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): stop stale-blocked sweep and dep-graph refresh starving repos with real backlogs

## Done when

- [ ] A repo with a clean pass inside the interval is not re-listed, and the remaining due repos share the whole sweep budget.
- [ ] Partial and failed passes never stamp the repo; a partial pass never touches the global sentinel; missing or future-dated stamps keep a repo due.
- [ ] Dep-graph refresh gives each repo with entries `(budget - elapsed) / remaining active repos` seconds (minimum 1), smallest backlog first, so idle repos no longer reduce the share.
- [ ] The new tests fail against the previous implementation and pass with the change; existing stale-sweep, dep-graph, readiness and budget-priority suites pass; ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed` are clean.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
  - New `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_stamp <slug>`: `~/.aidevops/cache/stale-blocked-complete/<owner>__<repo>`; rejects slugs outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` (same `/` → `__` mapping as `_der_stale_cursor_file`).
  - New `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_fresh <slug> <interval> <now>`: true only for a readable stamp with `0 <= now - mtime < interval`; missing, unreadable or future-dated stamps make the repo due.
  - New `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_mark_complete <slug>`: best-effort `touch`; a write failure only keeps the repo due.
  - `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`: build the due list in rotation order, skip fresh repos, divide the remaining budget by the due count, and stamp a repo only when `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` returns 0. Log `fresh_repos=<n>` in the summary line.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` — `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`: list repos as `<entry_count>\t<slug>` sorted by count then slug; count active repos (entries > 0); for each active repo `share = (budget - elapsed) / active_left`, minimum 1s.

- `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due` 59 → 76 lines; three new helpers of 6–9 lines; `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` 34 → 45 lines. All below the 100-line gate.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due` is called once per cycle from `pulse-wrapper.sh` under `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` is called from the in-cycle pipeline after `build_dependency_graph_cache` (`pulse-wrapper.sh`), from `_pulse_run_blocker_refresh_catchup` (`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) and from `normalize_repo_dependency_readiness` with a one-repo graph (`pulse-dep-graph.sh`). Unblock decisions remain `_der_try_unblock` (stale sweep) and `_refresh_try_unblock_issue` (graph refresh), unchanged; `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues`, its cursor, batch limit and deadline contract, `_refresh_graph_repo` and `DEP_GRAPH_REFRESH_MAX_CANDIDATES` are untouched.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh` (sweep cadence, rotation, fair share, stage wiring) and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh` (bounded traversal, cursor, elapsed budget); runtime evidence is the sweep summary and `dep-graph-cache: refresh` lines in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no schema or config file changes; `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_INTERVAL`, `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and `DEP_GRAPH_REFRESH_BUDGET_SECS` keep their meaning and defaults.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`.

- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; older code ignores `~/.aidevops/cache/stale-blocked-complete/`, and deleting it only makes every repo due again.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`, add `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_stamp`, `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_fresh` and `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_mark_complete` above `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`.
2. In `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`, build the due list in rotation order (skipping fresh repos), share the remaining budget by the due count, stamp only on return 0, and add `fresh_repos=` to the summary line.
3. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`, sort repos by entry count, count active repos, and recompute each active share from the time left.
4. Extend both existing test scripts with the cases listed above, confirm the new cases fail against the previous implementation, then run the Verification Before Dispatch commands.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the mkdir-based pulse instance lock (`acquire_instance_lock`, `pulse-wrapper.sh`) allows one sweep at a time; stamps are single `touch` calls, and a stamp racing a manual run can only make a repo due early or late by one interval.
- **Migration/rollback:** no ordering requirement; deploy and revert are both safe at any point because a missing stamp means due, and old code never reads stamps.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners ignore stamps and sweep every repo as today; the summary log line only gains a trailing `fresh_repos=` field, which no code parses.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a repo is skipped only after a clean, complete pass inside the configured interval, the cadence the global sentinel already promised; partial and failed passes stay due and retry next cycle as today. `/` → `__` stamp names match the existing stale cursor files, and GitHub owners cannot contain `_`, so names do not collide.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a killed sweep leaves stamps only for repos that finished cleanly and persists the rotation offset before each start, so the next cycle resumes with the remaining due repos; unreadable or future-dated stamps make a repo due; a stamp write failure only keeps the repo due. The dep-graph refresh still checks elapsed time before each new candidate and visits at least one.

- **Runtime:** after deployment, sweep summaries report a growing `fresh_repos` count and a shrinking `partial_repos` count over consecutive cycles until the sentinel is touched; dep-graph refresh lines for repos with entries report `budget_secs` above 1.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

- **Conversation context:** Found while maximising worker throughput for a managed private repo's enrichment backlog: after t18662 the reconciler could release dependency-ready issues, but the two periodic recovery stages reached that repo's backlog at about one issue per cycle.

## What

Both periodic recovery stages spend their time budget on repos that still have work:

1. **Stale-blocked sweep** (`_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`): each repo records its own completion stamp after a clean, complete pass. A repo whose stamp is younger than `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_INTERVAL` is not re-listed; the sweep budget is shared only among due repos (partial, failed or never swept). The global sentinel, rotation offset, fair-share deadlines and hard stop keep their current meaning.
2. **Dep-graph refresh** (`refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`): `DEP_GRAPH_REFRESH_BUDGET_SECS` is shared only among repos with dependency entries. They run smallest backlog first, and each share is recomputed from the time actually left, so unused time rolls forward to the largest backlog. Repos without entries keep a 1s share; they do no candidate work.

## Why

Pulse log evidence (2026-10-11):

- **Stale sweep never converges.** The last 8 sweep summaries report `failures=0 partial_repos=31..51 repos=57`. The sweep budget is about 45s (`PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` 60 minus the 15s margin) split across all 57 repos, so the integer share is 0–1s. `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` stops after its first visit once the share deadline passes, so repos with only 2 candidates log `visited=1 ... complete=false`. Because some repo is always partial, the global sentinel is never touched and every cycle re-lists every repo, including repos that already finished. The managed private repo with ~340 blocked candidates advanced one issue per visit.
- **Dep-graph refresh share rounds down to 1s.** The graph cache holds 57 repos, but only 6 have `blocked_by` entries (162 entries, the largest has 152). The 30s budget is divided by all 57 repos (`30 / 57 = 0`, clamped to 1), so recent full-cycle refresh lines all log `budget_secs=1`; the 153-candidate repo logs `visited=1 ... complete=false` on each refresh, as does a 6-candidate repo. Repo-scoped refreshes (`normalize_repo_dependency_readiness`) build a one-repo graph and keep the full budget.

Neither stage changes what is released; both only control how quickly dependency-ready issues are found. Close events (`reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure`) remain the primary release path; these stages recover missed events.

## Context & Decisions

- Per-repo stamps instead of a smaller global sentinel: the global sentinel can only mark a traversal of all repos, which one large backlog prevents indefinitely.
- Failed passes stay due, as today, so transient listing failures retry on the next cycle; once no repo is partial the global sentinel still rests the whole sweep for the interval.
- Smallest-first ordering for the graph refresh is deterministic, and it lets each small backlog finish its batch before the largest one takes the remaining time. Ordering within the stale sweep keeps the persisted rotation.
- Not in scope: raising stage timeouts, batch limits or dispatch capacity; host CPU gate tuning; changing what either stage releases.

## Outcome

fix(auto-update): stop Pulse-run auto-updates rolling back every verified release

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `auto-update deployment incomplete runtime bundle rollback agents_stale` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: no open PRs touch `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`; no open or closed issue reports the rollback. The bundle check was added in 48a522d013 (2026-07-11); last helper change 41d9b663f2 (t18626)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main f8bb961c48: `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root`, `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_valid`, `_cmd_check_perform_update` (`.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`); `pin_aidevops_active_runtime_bundle_root` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-runtime.sh`); Pulse pin export (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — one-function fix in update verification; setup, activation and rollback mechanics unchanged
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found while verifying that a released Pulse fix was running: v3.39.8, v3.39.9 and v3.39.10 each deployed, passed setup, then were rolled back by the automatic updater one second after `SETUP_COMPLETE`.

## What

Post-update verification checks the bundle behind the global activation link (`~/.aidevops/agents`), whichever process runs the update. `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root` stops resolving the caller's inherited `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pin, so a Pulse-run update (routine r902) verifies the bundle it just activated instead of the Pulse's own older bundle.

## Why

- `pulse-wrapper.sh` exports `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pinned to its own physical bundle (`pwd -P`). Routine r902 runs `aidevops auto-update check` as a Pulse child, so the pin is inherited; `aidevops.sh` keeps an inherited value.
- `_cmd_check_perform_update` runs setup (which re-binds to the activation link via `pin_aidevops_active_runtime_bundle_root`, and activates the new bundle correctly), then verifies with `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root`, which resolves the stale pin. The old bundle's `VERSION` never matches the new version, so every Pulse-run update logs `Update pulled vX but agents at vX — deployment incomplete` and rolls back to the bundle it just replaced. The launchd-scheduled path has a clean environment and succeeds, which is why some updates stick.
- Runner evidence (`~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log`): 84 same-version `deployment incomplete` rollbacks since 2026-07-23 against 30 `Update complete` lines since July; today v3.39.8, v3.39.9 and v3.39.10 all rolled back. Recovery only comes 3–7 minutes later from `_cmd_check_stale_agent_redeploy` (`Deployed agents stale ... re-deploying`).
- Cost per release on every runner: two extra full setup runs, two extra Pulse restarts that discard the in-flight dispatch cycle, and minutes of running the previous release. A manual `aidevops update` started in that window reports "already up to date" because it compares the version before the rollback lands.
- Local reproduction with the real functions in a sandbox HOME (activation link → new bundle): clean env → verification valid; Pulse-style pin → resolves the old bundle → `INVALID(rollback)`; CLI symlink pin → valid.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh` — `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root` resolves `${HOME}/.aidevops/agents` (the activation link) with `pwd -P`, ignoring an inherited `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR`; comment cites the Pulse pin and the matching rule in `pin_aidevops_active_runtime_bundle_root`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root` is called twice, both in `_cmd_check_perform_update`: `prior_bundle_root` (rollback target, now the bundle active before the update instead of the caller's pin) and `active_bundle_root` (verification). Sibling reads in the same flow already use `$HOME/.aidevops/...` (`deployed_version`, `_auto_update_rollback_runtime_bundle` previous link and bundles root).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** no new writes. Setup, activation, Pulse reconciliation and `runtime-bundle-rollback-helper.sh` are unchanged; a genuinely invalid or missing bundle still rolls back.
- **Existing verification/tests:** no test calls these functions (`rg '_auto_update_runtime_bundle' .agents/scripts/tests` is empty); `test-linux-lifecycle-smoke.sh` sets `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` equal to `$HOME/.aidevops/agents`, so it is unaffected.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no schema or config changes.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` into the runtime bundle.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the change only affects future update runs.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR to restore pin-based resolution.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Mixed-version:** the fix runs from the updater's own (old) bundle, so the first update to the release containing it may still roll back on a Pulse-run updater and self-heal through the stale-agent redeploy; updates after that verify correctly.
- **Custom agents directories:** the auto-updater already assumes the default layout (`INSTALL_DIR`, `deployed_version`, rollback links), so ignoring a custom `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` here removes an inconsistency rather than a feature.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-update-health-check.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cmd-update-sha-drift.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the sandbox reproduction (real functions, Pulse-style pin) must report `valid` for all three environments after the change; the existing auto-update suites cover the helper's other subcommands; ShellCheck and the changed-file linters cover the edit.
- **Runtime:** after this release is deployed, the next Pulse-run update logs `Update complete: vX -> vY (agents deployed)` with no `deployment incomplete` or `Rolled back runtime activation` line.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18664-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pinned to an older bundle and the activation link on the new bundle, post-update verification checks the new bundle and passes.
- [ ] A missing, unvalidated or version-mismatched active bundle still fails verification and rolls back.
- [ ] ShellCheck, the existing auto-update suites and `linters-local.sh --changed` pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Fix the verifier instead of unsetting the pin in the r902 wrapper: any caller with an inherited pin (Pulse routines, workers, interactive sessions) hits the same false negative, and setup already applies the activation-link rule for global reconciliation.
- Not in scope: rollback-helper behaviour, the stale-agent redeploy debounce, or setup's own pin handling.

- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — order-only change in one round orchestrator plus a runner-local stamp; every dispatch gate unchanged

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Enrichment throughput drive on a managed private repo: the runner sat at 0–2 of 20 worker slots for 12 cycles while that repo's available backlog was non-empty.

## What

`dispatch_max` orders each round so candidates attempted within a window without a worker launch go after the candidates of the same priority tier that were not attempted in that window; the recently attempted ones rotate oldest attempt first. A runner-local per-candidate stamp is written at `DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_ATTEMPT` and removed when a worker launch is confirmed.

## Why

- Rounds are bounded by the cycle wall-clock budget: a round stops taking candidates once less than the 600 s per-candidate floor remains. Two recent large rounds covered only a prefix of the ranked list — `processed=26/82` and `processed=28/80`, both `implementation_dispatched=0` and both ending with `Dispatch_max stopping early: cycle wall-clock budget below per-candidate floor` (28 such stops in the current `pulse.log`). Dedup layers alone took up to 144.5 s per attempt for the managed private repo below (p90 30.9 s; `dispatch-stages.tsv`, 9–11 Oct).
- The ranking is deterministic (priority tier, score, `createdAt`), and the benign-block ledger is deliberately cycle-local so stale active claims cannot suppress later cycles. Every round therefore re-attempts the same head candidates.
- Runner evidence (current `pulse.log`; read-only available-issue probe at 11:06Z): the managed private repo's top head candidates were attempted 15–23 times each (`blocked_by_unresolved`, `footprint_overlap`, `dedup_active_claim`, `consolidated`, `terminal_blocker_circuit`). Meanwhile 24 of its 47 `status:available` issues in the enrichment class (20 of them `auto-dispatch`) had never been attempted on this runner. 17 of those 24 are `tier:thinking`, which the score ranks 1200 points below `tier:standard`.
- Last 12 cycles (`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`, to 11:02Z): 0–2 of 20 workers active; 9 of the 12 dispatched nothing.
- Order-only rotation lets bounded rounds reach the untried tail without weakening any gate.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` — after `_dispatch_filter_capability_cooled_candidates`, following its per-candidate state pattern:
  - window knob `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_ATTEMPT_RECENCY_SECONDS` (default 86400, `0` disables, capped at 604800);
  - `_dispatch_attempt_recency_path`, `_dispatch_attempt_recency_stamp` (mktemp + mv), `_dispatch_attempt_recency_clear`;
  - `_dispatch_attempt_recency_stamps` (emit in-window stamps; remove expired, future-dated and malformed ones);
  - `_dispatch_order_attempt_recency_candidates`: one jq stable sort by `[-priority_rank, attempted, attempt epoch, original index]`. It fails open and emits one log line plus a stats counter when it demotes anything.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` — `_dispatch_process_candidate`: stamp after `attempt_epoch=$(date +%s)`; clear after `dispatch_worker_spawned`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — new `_dispatch_order_round_candidates` (recency order when loaded, then `_dispatch_order_idle_borrowing_candidates`); `dispatch_max` calls it in place of the direct idle-borrowing call.

### Complexity Impact

- `_dispatch_process_candidate`: 96 → 98 body lines (+2).
- `dispatch_max`: 99 → 99 (one call replaced).
- New functions each stay under 40 lines.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_dispatch_process_candidate` is the only attempt path for the floor, parallel and priority loops. `dispatch_max` runs every round:
  - via `apply_dispatch_max`: normal passes, event refills, preflight/post-label refills;
  - directly: `_dispatch_min_worker_floor_refill`, `maybe_refill_underfilled_pool_during_active_pulse` and `_run_early_exit_recycle_loop`.
  - The priority phases (`_dispatch_priority_phase_candidates`) and the floor/max loops consume candidates in input order.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** new runner-local soft state `~/.aidevops/cache/dispatch-attempt-recency/<owner>--<repo>--<issue>` (one epoch per file). No GitHub writes, and no label, claim, ledger or reservation changes.
- **Existing verification/tests:** the suites that drive `dispatch_max` or `_dispatch_process_candidate` isolate `HOME`, so they see no stamps and today's order.
- **Schemas/config:** one environment knob; no config file change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` into the runtime bundle.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Stamps start empty, so the first round after deploy keeps today's order and stamps what it attempts.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_ATTEMPT_RECENCY_SECONDS=0` disables the rotation; reverting the PR restores today's order; leftover stamps are inert once the code is gone.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Priority:** `priority:critical`/`priority:high` tiers still lead strictly (GH#32703). Only the order inside a tier changes, and score order is kept among candidates not attempted recently.
- **Retry latency:** a recently attempted, still-blocked candidate is retried after its tier's fresher candidates, and at most one window later (default 24 h).
- **Safety:** ordering only. Dedup, claim, footprint, dependency, capability, eligibility and budget gates are unchanged and still run for every attempted candidate.
- **Concurrency:** parallel candidate subshells write distinct files atomically; a prune race can only lose a stamp, which falls back to today's order.
- **Bash 3.2:** no associative arrays or `mapfile`.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** a scratch harness sources the real libraries under a sandbox `HOME` and checks:
  - no stamps → identical order;
  - stamps → fresh first within each tier, oldest attempt first, critical tier still first;
  - expired, future-dated and malformed stamps are removed;
  - window `0` or malformed JSON → unchanged order.
- **Pre-existing failure:** `test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh` fails 4/21 identically on an untouched `git archive` of origin/main 51296462a4. The secret-name gate from #32748 preempts the expected skip lines; tracked by t18666 (GH#34364).
- **Runtime:** after deploy, `pulse.log` shows the rotation line. On a later private-repo wave, the read-only available-issue probe shows previously never-attempted candidates being attempted and some launching.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18665-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A candidate attempted without a launch inside the window is ordered after every not-recently-attempted candidate of its priority tier, and recently attempted candidates rotate oldest attempt first.
- [ ] `priority:critical`/`priority:high` candidates still lead lower tiers regardless of stamps. With no stamps, or with the window set to `0`, round order is identical to today's.
- [ ] A confirmed launch removes the stamp. Expired, future-dated and malformed stamps are removed, and any state or jq failure returns the original order.
- [ ] ShellCheck, the listed dispatch suites and `linters-local.sh --changed` pass, apart from the pre-existing silent-dispatch failures noted above, which must match base exactly.

## Context & Decisions

- **Order, don't skip:** a cross-cycle skip ledger was rejected. The benign-block ledger is cycle-local on purpose (active claims clear), and skipping could starve a candidate whose blocker cleared. Demotion keeps every candidate reachable and every gate authoritative.
- **Time window, not `updatedAt`:** Pulse housekeeping updates issues itself, so an `updatedAt` reset could re-promote the same heads every cycle.
- **Applied in `dispatch_max`, after the 120 s ranked snapshot:** stamps written by the previous round's parallel subshells take effect in the next round.
- **Not in scope:** cycle-budget reserve sizing for refill rounds and per-candidate ceremony cost. Each needs its own fresh evidence before a separate task.

title: t18667: fix(pulse): reserve the post-label refill's real dispatch admission budget so...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18667` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): reserve the post-label refill's real dispatch admission budget so pre-refill stages cannot spend it

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `post-label refill dispatch admission budget enumeration reserve` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open related PR or issue. Related history: GH#32259 (#32264, sized the post-label refill reserve at 600 s), GH#33560 (#33561, added the enumeration estimate to dispatch admission), GH#33944 (#34075, refill skips dependency normalization), GH#33737 (first-wave reserve for pre-dispatch stages), GH#34302 (#34306, bounded/resumable label maintenance)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main 8e0ba8c1c0: `_preflight_refill_reserved_timeout` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh:454`), `_preflight_post_label_refill_wall_clock_allows` (`:523`), `_preflight_post_label_refill` (`:555`); call sites `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1971`, `:1978`, `:1986`; admission `_dispatch_cycle_budget_admits_round` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:747`); estimator `_dispatch_enumeration_expected_seconds` (`:702`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — budget arithmetic in one preflight library; no dispatch gate weakened
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Enrichment throughput drive: the runner sat at 0–3 of 20 worker slots while the post-label refill, the cycle's second dispatch opportunity, never reached candidate enumeration.

## What

The post-label refill and the optional stages before it (label maintenance, trusted-NMR reconciliation) use the refill's real dispatch admission budget — finalise reserve + per-candidate floor + measured full-scan enumeration estimate (990 s with the 300 s cold estimate) — instead of the configured 600 s minimum:

- while the cycle can still admit the refill, optional stages are clamped to leave that budget plus a 60 s margin;
- once it cannot, they keep today's 605 s clamp;
- the refill's wall-clock gate requires the same budget, so it no longer starts a refill that admission must skip.

## Why

- `dispatch_max` enumerates only while `remaining − finalise ≥ floor + enumeration` (`_dispatch_cycle_budget_admits_round`, GH#33560): 990 s raw by default, 1093 s with the recent 403 s estimate. GH#32259 sized the post-label reserve and gate at 600 s before that admission reserve existed, and it was never raised.
- Current `pulse.log`: 26 of the 30 post-label refills that passed the 600 s gate were then skipped before candidate enumeration — `remaining=505–803s` (after the finalise reserve) against `floor=600s enumeration=300–448s`. The `Dispatch current-state guardrail` lines at those refills show 17–20 of 20 slots available.
- In the two recent cycles with fast first waves (172 s and 184 s), 1444 s or more remained when label maintenance started. Label maintenance (527–555 s) and trusted-NMR reconciliation (103–108 s) ran under the 605 s clamp and left the refill 790–814 s raw.
- Clamped stages also overran the 5 s margin by 6, 10 and 24 s (70 s with REST degraded), so even the 600 s gate skipped at 599/595/581/535 s.
- In both of those cycles the next dispatch admission was skipped with negative remaining (−10 s, −11 s), so a dead refill left the cycle with only its first wave.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
  - new `_preflight_post_label_refill_required_seconds`: max(configured minimum, finalise + floor + full-scan estimate), mirroring `_dispatch_cycle_budget_admits_round`. It uses the configured minimum when the admission reserve is disabled (`AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DISPATCH_BUDGET_RESERVE` ≠ 1), the estimator is not loaded, the cycle length is unknown, or the reserve could never fit one cycle.
  - `_preflight_refill_reserved_timeout`: reserve that budget + 60 s while the refill still fits; otherwise the configured minimum + 5 s (today).
  - `_preflight_post_label_refill_wall_clock_allows`: require the same budget.

### Complexity Impact

- New `_preflight_post_label_refill_required_seconds`: 17 body lines.
- `_preflight_refill_reserved_timeout`: 10 → 19 body lines.
- `_preflight_post_label_refill_wall_clock_allows`: +3 lines.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_run_preflight_stages` only (`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1971`, `:1978`, `:1986`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none — no state files, labels, claims or GitHub writes. Log line text is unchanged; `required=` now reports the real budget.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh` sources only the preflight library (no estimator), so its contracts keep the configured 600 s path. `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` uses a 2476 s estimate that exceeds the cycle, so it also keeps 600 s.
- **Schemas/config:** no new knob. `PULSE_POST_LABEL_REFILL_MIN_REMAINING_SECONDS` stays a lower bound; `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DISPATCH_BUDGET_RESERVE`, `DISPATCH_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT_FLOOR` and `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CYCLE_FINALISE_RESERVE_S` are read as admission reads them.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` into the runtime bundle.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR. `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DISPATCH_BUDGET_RESERVE=0` restores the 600 s path but also disables the admission reserve.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Optional work:** in cycles where the refill fits, label maintenance and trusted-NMR reconciliation get up to 445 s less. Label maintenance is bounded and resumable per key (GH#34302); trusted-NMR reconciliation runs every cycle.
- **No starvation for a refill that cannot run:** when the refill cannot fit, optional stages keep today's clamp and the gate skips the refill without invalidating the candidate snapshot.
- **Safety:** no dispatch, claim, dedup, trust or budget gate changes; admission stays authoritative.
- **Known limit:** the 60 s margin does not cover the 70 s overrun seen with degraded REST; that refill is skipped as today.
- **Bash 3.2:** no new constructs beyond those already used by the admission code.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** a scratch harness sources the real watchdog, candidates and preflight libraries under a sandbox `HOME` with a mocked clock (32 cases, Bash 5.3 and 3.2) and checks:
  - required-budget fallbacks;
  - stage clamp fits/defers/falls back;
  - gate decisions;
  - the gate matches `_dispatch_cycle_budget_admits_round` at every second of an 1800 s cycle (300 s and 403 s estimates);
  - a replay of the 172 s first-wave cycle: legacy admits the refill at 600 s and admission then skips it; the new path reaches enumeration with 951 s.
- **shfmt advisory:** pre-existing `case` formatting in untouched label-maintenance code.
- **Runtime:** after deploy, `pulse.log` shows either `Post-label dispatch_max: refilling` with enumeration proceeding, or `Post-label dispatch_max skipped: insufficient wall-clock budget (... required=990s)`. An admitted refill should no longer be followed by `Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration`.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18667-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] While the cycle can still admit the refill, label maintenance and trusted-NMR reconciliation leave finalise + floor + full-scan estimate + 60 s; otherwise they keep today's configured-minimum clamp.
- [ ] The refill gate admits exactly when `_dispatch_cycle_budget_admits_round` would admit before enumeration at the same instant. It falls back to the configured minimum when the admission reserve is disabled, the estimator is unavailable, or the reserve exceeds the cycle.
- [ ] `PULSE_POST_LABEL_REFILL_MIN_REMAINING_SECONDS` remains a lower bound; an invalid value still skips with `wall-clock budget unavailable`.
- [ ] ShellCheck, the listed suites and `linters-local.sh --changed` pass.

## Context & Decisions

- **Mirror, don't call:** `_dispatch_cycle_budget_admits_round` logs and counts a skip, so the preflight repeats its arithmetic instead of probing it.
- **Fall back when the refill cannot fit:** holding the full reserve would starve optional work for a refill that admission will skip anyway.
- **60 s margin:** observed overruns of 6–24 s plus 2–5 s between the gate and admission; the 70 s degraded-REST overrun is accepted.
- **Not in scope:** first-wave duration (754–1996 s in most recent cycles, which is why most refills cannot fit), trusted-NMR reconciliation starving behind label maintenance, and the end-of-cycle dispatch budget. Each needs its own evidence before a separate task.

</details>

title: t18668: fix(pulse): restore footprint defer suppression for bodiless candidate snapsh...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18668` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): restore footprint defer suppression for bodiless candidate snapshots and size its TTL to the reconsideration gap

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `footprint defer suppression candidate body TTL pulse dispatch` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open related PR or issue. Related history: GH#30619 (6e0f2e0ed0, introduced the durable defer and its suppression), GH#32977 (same-batch footprint reservations), GH#33293 (claimed no-auto-dispatch coordinator exclusion), GH#33998 (shorter reservation critical section)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main 3ffa1d564a: `_footprint_defer_should_suppress` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:264`), `_FOOTPRINT_DEFER_TTL_SECONDS` (`:50`); caller `_dispatch_skip_for_footprint_defer` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:286`) from `_dispatch_process_candidate` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:548`); candidate snapshot fields (`.agents/scripts/pulse-repo-meta.sh:327`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — one dispatch-dedup module plus its diagnostics rule; no dispatch, claim or trust gate weakened
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Enrichment throughput drive, following t18665 (attempt-recency ordering) and t18667 (post-label refill budget). Footprint-deferred candidates were re-running the full dispatch ceremony every time a wave reached them.

## What

`_footprint_defer_should_suppress` works with the candidate JSON that Pulse actually passes it:

- When the candidate JSON has no `body`, it reads the candidate issue body instead of treating the missing body as a changed footprint. An unreadable candidate falls through to the live check without ending the defer.
- Local expiry is checked before any GitHub read.
- A blocker that became a `parent-task` or claimed `no-auto-dispatch` coordinator wakes the defer (`blocker_coordinator_recheck`), so the live check applies its coordinator exclusions.
- Each suppression logs `[footprint-defer] event=suppressed ...`, and `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` gains a `pfd-suppressed` rule.
- The default TTL rises from 1800 s to 21600 s. `AIDEVOPS_FOOTPRINT_DEFER_TTL_SECONDS` still overrides it.

## Why

- Candidate snapshots are listed with `number,title,url,assignees,labels,createdAt,updatedAt` (`pulse-repo-meta.sh:327`), with no body. That was already true when GH#30619 shipped. `.body // ""` gives an empty footprint, so every reconsideration woke with `candidate_footprint_changed`.
- `pulse-stats.json` (8-day retention): `dispatch_candidate_blocked_footprint_overlap` 681, `dispatch_candidate_footprint_defer_suppressed` 0.
- `pulse.log` (66.1 h): 342 deferrals and 305 wakes (297 `candidate_footprint_changed`, 8 `lifecycle_invalidation`). 246 of the spurious wakes were re-deferred against the same blocker after the full candidate ceremony (repo refresh, metadata fetch, dedup layers, large-file gate). Wake to re-defer took p50 78 s and p90 147 s, 21,735 candidate-seconds in total. 267 of the 342 deferrals were in a managed private repo.
- TTL: at those reconsiderations the defer was p25 7,449 s, median 10,593 s and p75 15,087 s old. A 1800 s TTL covered 5% (11/237), 21600 s covers 89% and 43200 s covers 100%.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
  - new `_footprint_defer_candidate_body`: use a string `body` from the candidate JSON, otherwise `gh_issue_view <N> --json body` (raw `gh` when the wrapper is not loaded); non-zero when unreadable.
  - new `_footprint_defer_blocker_wake_reason`: `blocker_lifecycle_changed` (not open or no active status label), `blocker_coordinator_recheck` (`parent-task`, or `no-auto-dispatch` + `status:claimed`), `blocker_footprint_changed`; empty while the blocker still holds the recorded footprint.
  - `_footprint_defer_should_suppress`: force-dispatch → expiry → candidate body/hash → blocker; log `event=suppressed`.
  - `_FOOTPRINT_DEFER_TTL_SECONDS` default 21600.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` — `pfd-suppressed` rule; refresh the `pfd-deferred`/`pfd-wake` line references.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` — the `gh` mock serves candidate bodies, an extra blocker label and a call log; Tests 20–24 use a production-shaped candidate snapshot.

### Complexity Impact

- `_footprint_defer_should_suppress`: 63 → 61 body lines (blocker evaluation moved to a helper).
- New `_footprint_defer_candidate_body`: 15 body lines. New `_footprint_defer_blocker_wake_reason`: 23 body lines.
- `complexity-regression-helper.sh check` reports 0 new violations for function-complexity, nesting-depth and bash32-compat.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_dispatch_skip_for_footprint_defer` only. `_footprint_defer_status_json` and `pulse-diagnose-issue.sh` display records whose schema is unchanged. No consumer branches on specific `wake_reason` values.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** defer state files under `~/.aidevops/cache/footprint-defers/` (schema v1; `suppressed_count`/`last_checked_at` as before) and new `event=suppressed` lines in `pulse.log`. No labels, claims, comments or other GitHub writes.
- **GitHub reads:** each non-expired suppression check reads the candidate body (one REST-capable `gh_issue_view`) and the blocker, which was already read. Before, each reconsideration ran the full candidate ceremony instead (metadata fetch, dedup layers, in-flight label lists, repo refresh).
- **Schemas/config:** only the `AIDEVOPS_FOOTPRINT_DEFER_TTL_SECONDS` default changes. Existing records keep their recorded `expires_at` and pick up the new TTL when re-deferred.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` into the runtime bundle.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR. `AIDEVOPS_FOOTPRINT_DEFER_TTL_SECONDS=1800` restores the old window.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Safety:** suppression skips a candidate only when its footprint is unchanged and its recorded blocker is still open, has an active status label, is not a coordinator, and has the footprint it had when the live check found the overlap. The live check would defer that candidate again.
- **Fail-closed blocker read (unchanged):** an unreadable blocker keeps suppressing as GH#30619 designed. The TTL and event-driven `lifecycle_invalidation` (issue close, PR merge, claim release) bound this.
- **Known divergence:** the live in-flight read lists at most 50 open issues per status label. A recorded blocker outside that window keeps suppressing until the TTL ends. This is conservative: it never admits an overlap.
- **Longer TTL:** every suppression re-reads the candidate and blocker, and close/merge/release events wake defers immediately. The TTL only bounds drift that those reads cannot see (low-information basename config, extraction changes, blocker-read outages).
- **Bash 3.2:** no new constructs; the suite passes on `/bin/bash` 3.2.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh
/bin/bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-diagnose-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main --working-tree --metric function-complexity
```

- **Regression proof:** run against the origin/main module, 4 of the 5 new production-shaped cases fail. The Test 20 failure is the live symptom: `wake_reason=candidate_footprint_changed` at age 0.
- **Runtime:** after deploy, `pulse.log` should show `[footprint-defer] event=suppressed` and `pulse-stats.json` a non-zero `dispatch_candidate_footprint_defer_suppressed`. `candidate_footprint_changed` wakes followed by a same-blocker re-defer within 900 s should fall toward zero (`defer_age.py`-style pairing).
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18668-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A candidate snapshot without `body` and with an unchanged footprint is suppressed while its recorded blocker is open, in flight, not a coordinator and unchanged.
- [ ] An unreadable candidate falls through to the live check without tombstoning the defer.
- [ ] An expired defer wakes before any GitHub read.
- [ ] A `parent-task` or claimed `no-auto-dispatch` blocker wakes the defer with `blocker_coordinator_recheck`.
- [ ] The default TTL is 21600 s, and `AIDEVOPS_FOOTPRINT_DEFER_TTL_SECONDS` still overrides it.
- [ ] ShellCheck, the footprint suite on Bash 5 and 3.2, the diagnose suite and the complexity gates pass.

## Context & Decisions

- **Read the body; don't widen the snapshot:** adding `body` to the candidate listing would enlarge every cycle's listing for every open issue, only to serve the few candidates with an active defer.
- **Read rather than infer from `updatedAt`:** label and comment activity also bumps `updatedAt`, so it would only sometimes save the read and adds a stale-snapshot edge case.
- **21600 s, not 43200 s:** covers 89% of the observed reconsiderations and keeps a 6 h backstop for drift the per-check reads cannot see.

title: OAuth pool status counts auth-error accounts as available despite Pulse excluding them
body:
## Outcome

Make OAuth pool status report effective dispatch eligibility rather than counting an auth-error account as available solely because its cooldown is absent or expired. Diagnostic-only fix; do not weaken Pulse admission or reset credentials/cooldowns.

## Verified premise

Current upstream `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_accounts.py:184-209` and the deployed implementation have the same predicate: `available` only checks `cooldownUntil`. In contrast, `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:79-113` explicitly excludes `status == "auth-error"` from available accounts, independent of cooldown.

Synthetic credential-free input to the existing `pool_ops.py status-stats` entry point:

```json
{"anthropic":[{"status":"auth-error","cooldownUntil":0}]}
```

With `NOW_MS=100000`, `PROV=anthropic`, observed output is Total accounts 1, Available now 1, Active/idle 0, Rate limited 0, Auth errors 1. The auth-error account is not actually dispatch-eligible under Pulse's predicate. No live credentials are needed to reproduce.

A zero-capacity incident exposed this misleading status. Later the cached capacity command returned 1 maximum / 0 active / 1 available without a manual reset. This report does NOT establish an ongoing dispatch outage, a revoked token, or a new failure of auto-refresh recovery. `pulse-wrapper.sh --command capacity` reads the preflight-written target; it is not itself a fresh provider probe. A healthy token endpoint also does not prove an individual account is authenticated.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed aidevops issues for pulse auth capacity, pool available auth-error, auth-error, status-stats, Available now/auth and availability/auth-error. Related closed issues: #32927 (expired auth-error recovery), #32960 (bounded auto-refresh and alert), #30024 (tier routing with only auth-error accounts). Their recovery/routing objectives are distinct from this surviving status-statistics predicate. Current upstream code was checked before filing. Recheck PRs/issues before implementation to avoid parallel fixes.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_accounts.py`
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/tests/test_pool_ops.py`

## Reference pattern and constraints

Use `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh::_pulse_capacity_provider_account_counts` as the effective eligibility reference and inspect the existing account-selection predicate before deciding malformed/unknown-status behavior. Preserve status-stats CLI labels and output structure, account totals and auth/rate-limited counts. Do not edit deployed mirrors, Pulse gating, pool credentials, provider settings, refresh behavior or auto-clear behavior. If shell `cmd_status` normalization affects semantics, inspect `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-manage.sh:682-741` but do not expand mutation scope without evidence.

Replace the generic zero-availability advice only if necessary to avoid implying that manually clearing auth errors validates credentials; distinguish auth recovery from rate-limit cooldowns without introducing a bypass.

## Acceptance and verification

- auth-error accounts with cooldown missing, null, zero, expired or future are not reported dispatch-available.
- Active/idle accounts and expired rate-limited accounts retain the existing dispatch-eligibility behavior; future rate limits remain unavailable.
- Mixed pools report consistent available/auth-error/rate-limited totals.
- Add focused coverage in the existing test module; use synthetic stdin and fixed timestamps, never real tokens/network endpoints.
- Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/tests -p test_pool_ops.py` and the existing focused Python lint command for changed files.
- Re-run the existing `pool_ops.py status-stats` entry point with synthetic input and compare effective availability to Pulse's reference predicate. No new runner, broad CI gate or live account mutation.

## Tier and recovery

Tier standard: known diagnostic inconsistency, bounded Python reporting change with semantic comparison and existing coverage. Rollback is a plain revert; no state/schema migration. Return a verified PR; preserve normal merge/review gates.

body:
**Task ID:** `t18669` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): stop footprint extraction turning EDIT/NEW prose and template placeholders into shared file claims

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `footprint extract paths false overlap release intent claim-task-id interactive brief` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open or recently merged related PR. Related history: GH#27787 (intent-aware extraction), GH#28861 (`File:` needs its colon), GH#32977 (Files Scope list items), GH#33522 (low-information root files), t18668 (defer suppression)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main d3afddd46d: `_footprint_extract_paths` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:744`); consolidation instruction text (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh:86`, `:103`); defer hashes built from extracted paths (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:314`, `:357`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — one extraction pipeline in one dispatch-dedup module; no dispatch, claim or trust gate weakened
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Pulse throughput investigation after t18668 restored footprint defer suppression. Defer records showed unrelated issues deferring each other on paths such as `wildcard` and `regressions.`.

## What

`_footprint_extract_paths` stops reading two kinds of text as file claims:

- An `EDIT` or `NEW` marker without its colon, followed by a bare word. Without the colon, a marker now declares only a backtick- or quote-wrapped path, as in ``- NEW `tests/x.mjs` ``.
- Template placeholders: tokens containing `<`, `>`, `{` or `}`, or starting `path/to/`.

Every other declaration is extracted exactly as before, including colon declarations anywhere on a line.

## Why

- The extractor matched an `EDIT`/`NEW` marker with an optional colon anywhere in the body, so prose became a claim: "Inherited NEW wildcard lines" gave `wildcard`, "EDIT-to-NEW regressions." gave `regressions.`, "NEW JSON parts under" gave `JSON`, "EDIT only" gave `only`. Quoted examples gave `path/to/file` and `todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`.
- Pulse inlines the consolidation instructions (`pulse-triage-dispatch.sh:86`, `:103`) into every consolidated issue. Every consolidated issue therefore claimed `regressions.`, `path/to/file` and the `<area>` path, and one in flight deferred the others.
- Defer records on this runner (243 since 2026-08-24): 28 deferrals rested only on such tokens, and 6 more included one. 21 of the 28 are in a managed private repo. There, one in-review issue with an open PR is the recorded blocker of 6 deferrals through `wildcard`. In 4 of them `wildcard` was the candidate's only overlap with any in-flight issue; the other 2 also share real paths with other in-flight issues, because `_footprint_find_overlap` lists every overlapping path but names only the owner of the last match. At 14:35Z, 2 of the 4 live deferrals in that repo were `wildcard`-only, with about 5.5 h of their 6 h TTL left. The other 7 are in this repo (`only`, `if`, `the`, `declarations`, `(conditional)`).

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:744-777` — `_footprint_extract_paths`: a colon marker keeps its optional opening backtick or quote; a colon-less `EDIT`/`NEW` must be followed by one. A new `grep -vE` stage drops tokens with `<`, `>`, `{` or `}`, or starting `path/to/`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` — Test 6b: consolidation prose, quoted examples and placeholders yield nothing. Combined (`NEW/EDIT:`), repeated, bold, numbered, `### File:` heading, glob and colon-less backticked declarations are kept.

### Complexity Impact

- `_footprint_extract_paths`: one more pipeline stage and a longer comment. No new functions or branches.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_footprint_check_overlap` (candidate side), `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` (in-flight side), `_footprint_defer_should_suppress` and `_footprint_defer_blocker_wake_reason` (defer hashes). Both overlap sides use the same parser, so the check stays symmetric.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none new. A defer record whose candidate or blocker footprint loses a dropped token no longer matches its stored hash, so it gets the live check on the next reconsideration instead of waiting out its TTL.
- **Schemas/config:** none. `footprint_low_info_paths` and the low-information basenames are unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` into the runtime bundle.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Missed declarations:** a colon-less marker before an unquoted path (`- NEW todo/x.md`) is no longer read; none of the 928 task briefs in this repo has one. A real path containing `<`, `>`, `{` or `}`, or starting `path/to/`, would be dropped; none exists in that corpus. A missed overlap can at worst let two workers edit one file, which merge-conflict handling covers.
- **Glob declarations:** real glob lines such as `- NEW: todo/research/log/*/*/name-*.jsonl` are kept; only `<>{}` mark a placeholder.
- **Bash 3.2:** no new constructs; the suite passes on `/bin/bash` 3.2.57.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh
/bin/bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh
.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main --working-tree --metric function-complexity
```

- **Negative control:** the origin/main extractor returns the 9 real Test 6b paths plus `wildcard`, `regressions.`, `JSON`, `path/to/file`, `{path/to/new-file}` and two `<area>` paths.
- **Corpus:** over all 928 `todo/tasks/*-brief.md` files, origin/main yields 3131 brief/path pairs and the fix 3075: 56 dropped, 0 added. Every dropped token is a prose word, a placeholder or a brace-expansion prefix the old regex cut at its comma (`extraction-schemas/{invoice`).
- **Live issues:** 28 of 446 open issues in the private repo change, and 1 of 50 across 8 other managed repos. Every removed token is prose or a placeholder; nothing is added.
- **Runtime:** after deploy, `[footprint-defer] event=deferred` records should stop listing word or placeholder tokens, and the candidates they held should get a live check and dispatch or defer on real paths.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18669-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A colon-less `EDIT`/`NEW` before a bare word produces no footprint path.
- [ ] Tokens containing `<`, `>`, `{` or `}`, or starting `path/to/`, produce no footprint path.
- [ ] Colon declarations anywhere on a line, combined, bold, numbered and heading markers, globs, line qualifiers and colon-less markers before a backticked path are extracted as before.
- [ ] Over the repo's task briefs the change only drops tokens, and every dropped token is prose or a placeholder.
- [ ] ShellCheck, the footprint suite on Bash 5 and 3.2, and the complexity gate pass.

## Context & Decisions

- **Reject junk shapes, not unanchored declarations:** a first attempt only read declarations at the start of a line. The brief corpus showed it dropped real ones (combined markers, several per line, bold, `### File:` headings, colon-less backticked paths), so the fix keeps the original match and rejects only the two observed junk shapes.
- **Keep glob paths:** declared globs are real ownership claims in repositories that log per-run files, and the overlap check compares them as exact strings.
- **Not in scope:** rewording the consolidation instructions, which are correct prose; and quoted examples with realistic paths, such as a test-fixture body cited in a brief, which remain claims as before.

</details>

## Outcome

## Done when

- [ ] A sibling PR with more than 100 changed files no longer makes the open-siblings lookup uncertain.
- [ ] A truncated sibling PR is never exempt as planning-only.
- [ ] Partial label pages still fail the lookup (regression guarantee).
- [ ] ShellCheck and the has-open-pr suite on Bash 5 and 3.2 pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:258-325` — `_ddpr_graphql_open_siblings`: validate `files.pageInfo.hasNextPage` as a boolean instead of requiring `false`, and emit it per PR as `filesTruncated`. Keep `labels.pageInfo.hasNextPage == false`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:544-548` — `complete_planning_only_scope`: also require `filesTruncated` to be false, so a truncated PR is never exempt even if `changedFiles` disagrees with the page.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh` — the partial-connections test keeps its labels case; three new tests: a draft sibling with partial files blocks as a checkpoint, an oversized sibling that does not reference the issue no longer blocks it, and a truncated sibling whose first page looks planning-only still owns the issue.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` is the only caller (`rg -n _ddpr_graphql_open_siblings .agents/` finds the definition and one call). Its draft-checkpoint match reads title, body, labels and `isDraft`; its healthy-sibling match reads review/merge state, title, body and `complete_planning_only_scope`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because the lookup is a read-only GraphQL search; `has-open-pr` writes nothing on GitHub or local state.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh` encodes the lookup contract through `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh has-open-pr`; the production path is the same command and the pulse log `PR_LOOKUP_RESULT=uncertain ... scope=open_siblings` records.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because the new `filesTruncated` key exists only in the in-memory JSON passed from `_ddpr_graphql_open_siblings` to its caller; no config, cache or serialized format changes.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` on release/update; no generated copies.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored data or cache depends on the response shape; the next pulse cycle uses the new lookup.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because nothing is persisted; reverting `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` restores the strict check.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `_ddpr_graphql_open_siblings`, replace `.files.pageInfo.hasNextPage == false` with `(.files.pageInfo.hasNextPage | type) == $boolean_type`, keep the labels check, and add `filesTruncated: .files.pageInfo.hasNextPage` to the emitted object. Document the reasoning in the function header.
2. In `complete_planning_only_scope`, add `((.filesTruncated // false) | not) and` before the existing count checks. Keep it parenthesised: jq `|` binds looser than `and`.
3. In the test file, reduce the partial-connections test to its labels case and add the three tests named above to `main`, modelled on `test_has_open_pr_allows_when_no_healthy_sibling`.
4. Run ShellCheck and the suite on Bash 5 and `/bin/bash` 3.2, then the negative controls and the production-path check below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A because the change is a pure transformation of one API response inside one process; no locks, claims or shared files are touched.
- **Migration/rollback:** none needed; nothing persists the response, so deploy and rollback take effect on the next pulse cycle.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** producer and only consumer ship in the same file, so they cannot be mixed; older runners keep failing closed on oversized siblings until they update.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the lookup is read-only and repeatable; a retry returns the same decision for the same PR state.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** API errors, missing cost and partial labels still fail closed with `PR_LOOKUP_UNCERTAIN`; only a partial file page is now decided.
- **Planning-only exemption:** only complete file lists can exempt a sibling, as before; the new `filesTruncated` guard also covers a `changedFiles` count that disagrees with the page.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`
- **Current line count:** 86 lines (threshold: 100 lines for function-complexity)
- **Estimated growth:** +1 line

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh
```

- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

Related history: GH#32000 (same failure class for the open-commits lookup, fixed by paginating commits), t18131 / `fca5c68796` (moved this lookup from `gh pr list --json ...,files,labels` to response-metered GraphQL and added the `hasNextPage` checks)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main ae02c03740: `_ddpr_graphql_open_siblings` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:258`), its validation (`:301-309`), the only caller `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling` (`:484`, call at `:490`) and its `complete_planning_only_scope` (`:544-548`)

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Pulse throughput investigation. A high-priority issue in a managed private repo was rejected on every dispatch attempt with `PR_LOOKUP_UNCERTAIN: open_siblings lookup failed ... (reason=response_validation_failed)`.

## What

The open-siblings lookup accepts a sibling PR whose file list is longer than one page. It reports the partial page as `filesTruncated` instead of failing the whole response. A truncated PR is never exempt as planning-only, so it can still own the issue. Partial label pages still fail the lookup.

## Why

- `_ddpr_graphql_open_siblings` searches `repo:<slug> is:pr is:open #<issue>` and requests `files(first: 100)`. Its validator requires `files.pageInfo.hasNextPage == false` for every result, so one result with more than 100 changed files fails the lookup. `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling` then fails closed with `PR_LOOKUP_UNCERTAIN`, which blocks dispatch.
- GitHub search matches an issue number anywhere in a PR, including its comments. One large open PR therefore blocks every issue it mentions, on every cycle, even when its title and body do not reference that issue.
- Observed on this runner: the pulse log has 18 `open_siblings lookup failed ... (reason=response_validation_failed)` records, all for one `priority:high` `auto-dispatch` issue in a managed private repo, and 20 rejected dispatch attempts for it (`dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=1`) that took 14.7–65.8 s each, about 11.5 min in total. Its only search match is an open PR with 595 changed files and `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, whose title and body reference other issues only.
- The file list has one consumer: `complete_planning_only_scope`, which exempts a PR whose changed files are all `TODO.md` or `todo/**`. It already requires the returned file count to equal `changedFiles`, so a partial page could only ever keep a PR owning. Failing the lookup on it added no safety.
- Before t18131 the lookup used `gh pr list --json ...,files,labels` with no truncation check; the strict check arrived with the move to response-metered GraphQL.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a decided fail-closed policy inside one module with a verified reference pattern and focused tests; `dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` is not listed in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`, so no dispatch-path override applies.

## Context & Decisions

- **Mark truncation instead of paginating files:** GH#32000 paginated commits because commit headlines decide ownership. File paths here only grant the planning-only exemption, and a large PR is never planning-only, so extra pages would cost GraphQL quota and change no decision.
- **Keep labels strict:** partial labels could classify a protected draft as worker-owned and route it to continuation.
- **Not in scope:** narrowing the search to title/body matches, and the 20-result search bound.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:258` — `_ddpr_graphql_open_siblings`, the lookup and its validator
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:484` — `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling`, the only caller

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** dispatch of issues that GitHub search links to an open PR with more than 100 changed files
