title: t18672: fix(worker-lifecycle): stop the fix-the-fixer log watcher deadlocking workers...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18672` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(worker-lifecycle): stop the fix-the-fixer log watcher deadlocking workers before model invocation

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `verbose lifecycle watcher command substitution hang fix-the-fixer worker wedged` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no recent commits, merged or open PRs on `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-verbose.sh`
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main 9b61091128: `_start_verbose_lifecycle_watcher` (`.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-verbose.sh:83`), its only caller `_start_run_attempt_observers` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-attempt.sh:337`), cleanup (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:346`) and the only enabler (`headless-runtime-helper.sh:431`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — one function in one module, behaviour proven by a process-level probe on Bash 3.2 and 5.3
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Pulse throughput investigation. A `fix-the-fixer` worker for marcusquinn/cloudron-netbird-app#165 held a worker slot for over five hours without starting its model.

## What

A worker whose issue carries `fix-the-fixer` starts its model immediately after the verbose lifecycle watcher starts, and the watcher and its log follower exit when the worker exits, when cleanup stops them, after the watch timeout, or once all four checkpoints fire.

## Why

- `_start_run_attempt_observers` captures the watcher PID with `_t3077_watcher_pid=$(_start_verbose_lifecycle_watcher "$output_file" "$$" 2>/dev/null)`. The function backgrounds the watcher subshell without redirecting its stdout, so the subshell inherits the command-substitution pipe. The capture waits for EOF on that pipe; the watcher waits for lines in the worker log; the model that writes them starts only after the capture returns. Deadlock.
- Every loop exit (worker gone, timeout, four checkpoints) was checked only after a line arrived, so nothing could release it.
- Live evidence on this runner: wrapper PID 76334 for #165 last logged `pre_attempt_observers_start` at 2026-10-11T10:44:27Z and had no `post_attempt_observers_start` five hours later. `lsof` shows the wrapper's fd 3 is the read end of a pipe whose write end is fd 1 of watcher PID 98795; the watcher's `tail -F` follows a 0-byte worker log. Its 180s fix-the-fixer activity watchdog never armed, because it starts after model launch.
- #170 in the same repo wedged at the same stage from 2026-10-10T21:38:24Z until its exit trap recorded `reason=worker_runtime_not_invoked last_stage=pre_attempt_observers_start` at 23:44:59Z. Both fix-the-fixer dispatches in the retained worker logs wedged; the 56 other retained worker logs all passed the stage.
- The `tail -F` follower also leaked: cleanup sent TERM to the watcher, which killed the subshell but not the follower, and a follower writing to a pipe without a reader only dies on its next write. One follower from 2026-10-03 was still running eight days later on a 0-byte log.
- `fix-the-fixer` is applied to issues whose workers already failed, so every such repair attempt wedged a slot for hours and recorded another failure.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a narrow process-plumbing fix in one function with a verified mechanism (lsof pipe identity) and a reproducible probe; the module is not listed in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-verbose.sh:83-143` — redirect the watcher subshell's stdout to `/dev/null`; read with `read -t` on a poll interval (`AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE_WATCH_POLL_SECONDS`, default 5) so worker exit and the timeout are checked without log lines; start the follower as `sh -c 'printf "%s\n" "$$"; exec tail -F -n 0 "$1"'` so the watcher learns its PID; stop the follower on every exit path and from a TERM trap.
- `NEW: _verbose_lifecycle_stop_follower` in the same file — validates the PID before `kill` (never signals an empty or non-numeric target) and is safe under `set -e`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_start_run_attempt_observers` (`headless-runtime-attempt.sh:337`) is the only caller; `_cleanup_verbose_lifecycle_watcher` (`:346`) reads `watcher.pid` from the sentinel directory. `rg -n "_start_verbose_lifecycle_watcher|_cleanup_verbose_lifecycle_watcher" .agents/scripts` finds no others.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the watcher writes only sentinel files and runtime events through `_emit_verbose_checkpoint`; `_emit_worker_runtime_event` sends its own output to `/dev/null`, so discarding the watcher's stdout loses nothing. The `[lifecycle]` lines it prints go to stderr, which the caller already discards.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh` (structural plus checkpoint opt-in behaviour). It is not wired into CI.
- **Schemas/config:** new optional env `AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE_WATCH_POLL_SECONDS` (positive integer, default 5); `AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE_WATCH_TIMEOUT` keeps its meaning and is now enforced.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to the runtime bundle on release/update; no generated copies.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because nothing is persisted. Workers already wedged on an older bundle stay wedged; recover them separately after deployment.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting the file restores the old behaviour, deadlock included.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `_verbose_lifecycle_stop_follower`.
2. In `_start_verbose_lifecycle_watcher`, validate the poll interval, set the TERM trap, read the follower PID from its first line, poll with `read -r -t`, and treat a failed read as a quiet interval only while the follower is alive (Bash 3.2 returns 1 for both timeout and EOF).
3. Redirect the subshell's stdout with `) >/dev/null &` and stop the follower after the loop.
4. Run ShellCheck, the observability suite, and the process probe below on `/bin/bash` 3.2 and Bash 5.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** unchanged; one watcher per attempt, keyed by the wrapper PID.
- **Signal timing:** Bash 3.2 runs a trapped TERM only after the current `read -t` returns, so cleanup takes up to one poll interval; Bash 5 runs it immediately. The wrapper does not wait for the watcher.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** workers started by an older bundle keep the old code until they exit.
- **Partial lines:** a read timeout can split a line that arrives mid-poll and miss one checkpoint pattern. Checkpoints are best-effort diagnostics, so this is acceptable.
- **Load:** one `kill -0` and `date` per poll per fix-the-fixer worker.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_start_verbose_lifecycle_watcher` in `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-verbose.sh`
- **Current line count:** 61 lines (threshold: 100 lines for function-complexity)
- **Estimated growth:** +18 lines
- **Projected post-change:** 79 lines (79% of threshold)
- **Action required:** None — the follower stop is a separate 6-line helper.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** ShellCheck covers the edited module; the suite proves the module still loads and the checkpoint contract holds.
- **Process probe (Bash 3.2.57 and 5.3.20):** a wrapper with the production call shape (`set -euo pipefail`, `$(... 2>/dev/null)` capture) returned the watcher PID in 0s; all four runtime events fired; the watcher and follower were gone after four checkpoints, after cleanup TERM, after the wrapper exited without cleanup, and after a 3s watch timeout with a silent log.
- **Negative control:** the same probe against the deployed old module never returned from the capture until the watcher was killed externally.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — one module, no shared contract, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [x] Focused functional verification passes: process probe on Bash 3.2 and 5.3; `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh` (34/34)
- [x] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: t18672 verbose lifecycle watcher deadlock`
- [x] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required — single module

Initial implementation map. Directly necessary adjacent integration follows
`reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery".

**Hard boundaries:** do not change which issues enable verbose lifecycle, the checkpoint names, or the runtime event mapping; do not kill or redispatch live workers from this change.

**AI brief owner:** interactive maintainer session that filed this task.

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request
and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-verbose.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18672-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The background watcher does not hold the caller's command-substitution pipe.

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "^\t\) >/dev/null &$"
    path: ".agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-verbose.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Worker exit and the watch timeout are checked on a poll, without waiting for log lines.

## Context & Decisions

- **Redirect, not restructure:** callers keep `$(...)` for the PID; the fix is inside the function so no caller can reintroduce the pipe.
- **Polling over blocking reads:** a blocking read is what made worker exit and the timeout unreachable; a 5s poll costs almost nothing.

title: repos.json registry writes race under concurrent aidevops init (fixed .tmp path, no lock)
body:
## Problem

When two `aidevops init` runs happen at the same time (in different repos), one repo's registration update can be lost. Both runs write `repos.json` through the same fixed temp file `${REPOS_FILE}.tmp` with no lock. The second writer's `mv` fails, or it overwrites the first writer's update.

## Evidence (2026-10-11, aidevops v3.39.17)

- Two inits started in parallel from linked worktrees of two newly bootstrapped private repos.
- One printed `mv: <config>/repos.json.tmp: No such file or directory`.
- The other repo's entry was left with `features: []` and `version: "unknown"`, even though init reported success.
- Rerunning that init on its own repaired the entry.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh`: the fixed `${REPOS_FILE}.tmp` writers at lines 56, 67, 78, 525 and 622. Lines 704 and 744 already use `mktemp "${REPOS_FILE}.tmp.XXXXXX"`.
- Check other `repos.json` writers with `rg -n 'REPOS_FILE}\.tmp|repos\.json\.tmp' .agents/scripts`.

## Reference pattern

Use the `mktemp` writers at `aidevops-repos-lib.sh:704` and `:744`, plus a single registry lock (for example `mkdir`-based, as Bash 3.2 has no `flock`). Each read-modify-write must reread the file while holding the lock.

## Verification

Run two `aidevops repos maintenance on <repo>` (or init registration) commands concurrently against a temporary `REPOS_FILE` copy. Both updates must persist, no temp file may be left behind, and ShellCheck must pass.

### Files Scope

title: gh-write-helper.sh issue comment exits silently when the privacy guard blocks a public write
body:
## Problem

When the privacy guard blocks a body, `gh-write-helper.sh issue comment <N> --repo <public-repo> --body-file <file>` prints nothing and posts nothing. The caller can't see why it failed, and an agent reasonably retries or assumes it posted. Run the same body through raw `gh issue comment` (the shim) and it prints the reason clearly:

```text
[aidevops][privacy-scan][BLOCK] Write to public <repo> contains private-repo references: <basename> ...
```

## Evidence (2026-10-11, v3.39.17)

- Three wrapper attempts in a row printed nothing; the issue's comment list didn't change.
- The audit log (`audit-log-helper.sh tail`) had no `operation.block` entry for them.
- Raw `gh issue comment` with the same body printed the block reason above.
- An earlier wrapper call with a different privacy hit did print `[privacy-guard][BLOCK] ...`, so whether the reason shows depends on which guard path fires.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`: `gh_issue_comment` (around line 1302), `_gh_guard_public_write_args`, and the `_gh_with_timeout write` path. Find where the shim's privacy-scan stderr is discarded or where the function returns non-zero without a message.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`: make sure a non-zero result is reported (message on stderr, exit code passed through).

## Reference pattern

Raw `gh` through the aidevops shim already prints the block reason to stderr; the wrapper should pass it through unchanged and also record an `operation.block` audit event, as `_gh_edit_audit_rejection` in `shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` does.

## Verification

body:
**Task ID:** `t18673` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): read the exact PR when the prefetch snapshot is stale so worker draft-checkpoint dispatch hints work

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `dispatch negative cache worker draft checkpoint fingerprint prefetch snapshot` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open PRs on the target files; the last change to this hint was #33044 (GH#33034, 2026-09-29)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main 744fb55df3: `_dispatch_negative_pr_fingerprint` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:131`), its record caller (`:237`), its read caller (`:289`) and the prefilter call site that runs before the dispatch ceremony (`:541`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — two functions in one module plus focused cases in the existing suite
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Pulse throughput investigation. Candidates held by a worker draft checkpoint paid the full dispatch ceremony on every attempt, although a cross-cycle hint exists for exactly this case.

## What

When the last attempt on a candidate was blocked by a worker draft checkpoint, the next attempt inside the existing 30-minute hint window skips the candidate before the dispatch ceremony while the issue and the draft PR are unchanged, whether or not the batch-prefetch PR snapshot is fresh.

## Why

- `_dispatch_negative_pr_fingerprint` takes the PR revision (`updatedAt` + `headRefOid`) only from a complete batch-prefetch snapshot younger than 900s, at both record and read time.
- Prefetch rarely completes: early dispatch runs before `preflight_prefetch_and_scope` and spends the cycle budget (GH#33647, GH#34000). On this runner the PR snapshots completed at 00:42, 10:25, 12:44, 14:58 and 17:11Z on 2026-10-11.
- A hit therefore needs two attempts on the same candidate inside one 15-minute post-prefetch window. Observed re-attempt gaps are 14–413 minutes, so it almost never happens.
- Evidence (this runner, last 45,000 `pulse.log` lines, 2026-10-10T19:08Z–2026-10-11T17:12Z): 134 `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` rediscoveries cost 8,402 candidate-seconds (62.7s each) with zero `cross-cycle ownership block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` hits. The whole retained log has two hint hits, both `terminal_blocker_circuit`.
- Records are written when a snapshot happens to be fresh: 28 `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` records exist, the newest written about 15:05–15:12Z, minutes after the 14:58Z prefetch. None was ever read back.
- Replaying the logged attempt times with a fingerprint that is always available and the unchanged 1800s TTL skips 37 of 148 attempts (25%), about 2,300 ceremony-seconds per 22 hours on one runner. One managed private repo accounts for most of them.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a narrow fallback inside one module with a verified mechanism (snapshot age gate versus prefetch cadence) and focused cases in the existing suite. Dispatch-path module, so the change keeps every existing gate and stays skip-only.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:128-144` — keep the prefetch snapshot as the first source. A fresh complete snapshot stays authoritative: a PR missing from it is not open, so no hint and no API call. When the snapshot is missing, stale or incomplete, call the new REST reader.
- `NEW: _dispatch_negative_pr_rest_fingerprint` in the same file — one `timeout_sec`-bounded `gh api repos/{repo}/pulls/{pr}` read that returns `updated_at` + `_` + `head.sha` only for an open draft; any error returns 1. Model the field mapping on `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh:395-405` so both sources produce identical fingerprints.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:287-291` — check the TTL before reading the PR, so an expired hint costs no API call.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:66-80` — add `_DISPATCH_NEGATIVE_PR_REST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (env `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_NEGATIVE_PR_REST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default 10, range 1–30).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:838-841` — the GH#33538 parent-prefilter comment says "no API"; record the one bounded REST read a live worker-draft hint can now make there.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh:280-285` — the "stale snapshot cannot suppress dispatch" contract changes. Replace it with stale-snapshot cases for a failed read, an unchanged open draft (record and read), a closed PR and a ready PR, plus "fresh complete snapshot needs no read" and "expired hint costs no read".

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_dispatch_negative_pr_fingerprint` has two callers, `_dispatch_negative_cache_record` (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:237`) and `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` (`:289`); `rg -n "_dispatch_negative_pr_fingerprint" .agents/scripts` finds no others. `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` in turn runs in the parallel loop's parent prefilter (`_dispatch_max_prefilter_cached_block`, `:848`, called at `:798`, serial, before capacity checks) and in each candidate's own prefilter (`_dispatch_prefilter_owned_candidate`, `:307`, called at `:541` by every loop).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** records under `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-negative-cache/` keep their format; the fingerprint string is identical from either source.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` exercises `_dispatch_cache_confirmed_block` for other reasons.
- **Schemas/config:** one optional env var (above).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` on release/update; no generated copies.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none; existing records stay valid.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting the file restores the snapshot-only behaviour.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the timeout constant and `_dispatch_negative_pr_rest_fingerprint`.
2. Split `_dispatch_negative_pr_fingerprint` into "fresh complete snapshot → authoritative" and "otherwise → REST reader".
3. In the `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` read branch, check the TTL before the fingerprint read.
4. Update the suite, run ShellCheck and the suites below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Safety:** the hint only skips; it never launches, claims or relabels. The issue `updatedAt` match, the 1800s TTL and the exact PR revision match all still apply. Requiring an open draft from REST is stricter than the snapshot path.
- **Time-based transitions:** the GH#34008 expired-claim continuation and Layer 6 stale-assignment recovery change neither fingerprint, so a live hint can delay them by up to the unchanged 30-minute TTL, as designed in GH#33034.
- **API cost:** at most one REST core call per recorded block and per live hint read while the snapshot is stale (tens per cycle at most), versus the ceremony's many calls. The pulse puts the `gh` shim first on `PATH`, and the shim records the call, so the helper does not record it again.
- **Parent wave loop:** the GH#33538 parent prefilter runs serially before capacity checks, so a live worker-draft hint with a stale snapshot now costs one REST read there (typically under a second). This replaces the capacity wait, inter-launch delay and ~63s ceremony a spawned candidate would otherwise pay. Each read is bounded at 10s; a complete API stall costs at most 10s per hinted candidate, when every ceremony would be failing too. Keeping the parent local-only would forfeit the GH#33538 benefit (skip without spending a wave slot) for exactly these candidates.
- **Mixed versions:** older bundles keep reading the same record format.
- **Bash 3.2:** no new constructs.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- **Current line count:** 55 lines (threshold: 100 lines for function-complexity)
- **Estimated growth:** +3 lines
- **Projected post-change:** 58 lines (58% of threshold)
- **Action required:** None — the REST read is a separate helper of about 18 lines.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** the stale-continuation suite drives the real record and read functions with a stubbed snapshot helper and stubbed `gh`; the max-parallel suite covers the other cached reasons through the same recorder.
- **Live check after release and update:** `rg -c "cross-cycle (ownership )?block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` rises above 0 while repeated `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` rediscoveries for the same issues fall. The parent prefilter logs `cross-cycle block:`; the candidate prefilter logs `cross-cycle ownership block:`.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — one module, no shared contract, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required — single module

### Scope Boundaries

Initial implementation map. Directly necessary adjacent integration follows
`reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery".

**Hard boundaries:** do not change the TTL, the ownership gates, which reasons are cached, or the prefetch schedule.

**AI brief owner:** interactive maintainer session that filed this task.

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request
and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18673-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A missing, stale or incomplete PR snapshot falls back to one bounded exact-PR REST read.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "_dispatch_negative_pr_rest_fingerprint \"\\$repo\" \"\\$pr\""
    path: ".agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Only an open draft yields a REST fingerprint.

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "select\\(.state == \"open\" and .draft == true\\)"
    path: ".agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh"
  ```

- [ ] A fresh complete snapshot stays authoritative and expired hints are rejected before any PR read.

  ```yaml

    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh"
  ```

- [ ] After release and update, the runner logs `cross-cycle block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` (parent prefilter) or `cross-cycle ownership block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` (candidate prefilter) hits.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: manual
    prompt: "rg -c 'cross-cycle (ownership )?block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log is above 0 after the deploy"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Snapshot first:** free when fresh, and the only cheap proof that a PR is no longer open.
- **REST, not GraphQL:** the REST core budget is separate from the GraphQL budget the ceremony drains (same rationale as `_dispatch_skip_for_issue_body`).
- **TTL unchanged:** replayed hits rise to 82 of 148 at 7200s, but the expired-claim continuation and stale-assignment recovery are time-based and would wait up to the TTL. That trade-off needs its own decision.
- **Not in scope:** prefetch starvation (early dispatch before `preflight_prefetch_and_scope`), which also starves other snapshot consumers.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:251` — `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason`

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh:214` — record/read cases

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** nothing directly; reduces wasted dispatch ceremony for every runner
- **External:** none

title: hostinger fleet: sync fleet client domains into the privacy-guard entity list

## Problem

The privacy guard blocks private repo slugs in public GitHub writes. It only blocks client domains and site names if someone adds them by hand to `~/.aidevops/configs/privacy-guard-private-entities.txt` (`client:<value>` lines). That file doesn't exist on a fresh install. The hosting fleet inventory already lists every hosted domain, but nothing sends them to the guard, so client domains reached public issue bodies, task briefs and test fixtures without being blocked.

Add `hostinger-helper.sh fleet privacy-sync`, and run it automatically after `fleet inventory`. It should:

- read the private inventory and `~/.config/aidevops/hosting-fleet.json` (`site_repos`, `ignore`, owner);
- add `client:<domain>` entries for every fleet domain and site-repo name, and `repo` entries for fleet-owner repos, to the private entities file. Keep it mode 0600, keep manual entries, and don't create duplicates;
- skip owner-exception domains listed in config (for example, the owner's personal site);
- print only counts, never values.

title: Hook installers ignore core.hooksPath: gh-wrapper, quality, task-id and other guards never run in Beads repos
body:
## Problem

When `core.hooksPath` is set, Git runs hooks only from that directory. Beads sets it to `.beads/hooks`. Several aidevops installers ignore this and write to `<git-common-dir>/hooks/`, so their hooks are installed but never run.

On a Beads-enabled clone of this repo, `.git/hooks/pre-push` (gh-wrapper and quality checks) and `.git/hooks/pre-commit` exist but are never executed. `install-pre-push-guards.sh` had the same bug, so the privacy guard was inactive and private client names reached public history.

That installer is fixed in the linked PR. These remain:

| File | Lines (approx) |
|---|---|
| `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh` | 119-124, 216-221, 311, 371-376, 466-471, 528-532, 1335-1339, 1408-1429, help text 1720-1721 |
| `.agents/scripts/install-task-id-guard.sh` | ~63 (commit-msg) |
| `.agents/scripts/install-privacy-guard.sh` | legacy installer; ~20 |
| `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh` | 181-183 |
| `.agents/scripts/repo-verify-config-lib.sh` | 386-391 |

Second problem: `install-hooks-helper.sh` (gh-wrapper/quality pre-push) and `install-pre-push-guards.sh` (privacy/credential/scope pre-push) each manage the whole `pre-push` file. When one has written it, the other refuses with "unknown manager". The result is one set of guards or the other, never both.

## Proposal

1. Add one shared resolver, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` made absolute with `--show-toplevel` when relative, and use it in every installer above. The reference pattern is `_git_hooks_dir` in `.agents/scripts/install-canonical-guard.sh` and in `install-pre-push-guards.sh` after the linked PR.
2. Make the two pre-push managers coexist: either one dispatcher with sections for both, or each recognises the other's marker and chains it. Preserve a trailing Beads section the way `install-canonical-guard.sh` `_beads_section` does.
3. Add an `aidevops` health/status warning when an aidevops hook exists in `<common-dir>/hooks` while `core.hooksPath` points somewhere else (inactive hook).

## Verification

- In a temporary repo with `git config core.hooksPath .beads/hooks`: run each installer, then confirm the hook file is in `.beads/hooks` and that `git push`/`git commit` against a local bare remote actually executes it (for example, a guard that blocks a planted private-entity line).
- Run both pre-push installers in either order and confirm both guard sets are present and run.
- Without `core.hooksPath`, behaviour is unchanged: hooks go to `<common-dir>/hooks` and are shared across worktrees.

title: gh PATH shim masks a missing GitHub CLI in setup and issue-reporting helpers
body:
## Problem

When the GitHub CLI is not installed, the aidevops `gh` PATH shim hides that fact. In OpenCode the plugin puts the agents scripts directory first on `PATH`, so `command -v gh` resolves to the shim and succeeds. As a result:

- `setup_git_clis` never offers to install `gh`.
- `/log-issue-aidevops` and `framework-issue-helper.sh` pass their "installed" check and then fail inside the shim with `[aidevops] gh shim: real gh binary not found; aborting`, with no install guidance.

## Evidence

User report: `/log-issue-aidevops` failed with `[aidevops] gh shim: real gh binary not found; aborting`, while diagnostics reported `gh CLI: not installed`.

Code:

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install-discovery.sh:82` — `if ! command -v gh`.
- `.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh:172` and `.agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh:303` — same check.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:142,297,316,332` — "not found" messages without install steps.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-native-transport-lib.sh:59` `_find_real_gh` already resolves the native binary while skipping aidevops shims.

## How

- Detect the native binary (skip aidevops shims) in setup and both issue helpers, reusing the `_shim_is_aidevops_gh` path patterns.
- Add install and `gh auth login` guidance to the shim's not-found messages.

## Acceptance

- With only the shim on `PATH`, setup reports GitHub CLI missing and offers installation; the issue helpers print install guidance.
- With a real `gh`, behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification

ShellCheck on changed scripts; run the helpers with a `PATH` containing only the shim and confirm the messages.

title: One-time reset of raised OpenCode compaction targets to 240K (repeat of GH#32807)
body:
## Problem

GH#32807 reset raised OpenCode compaction targets to the 240K default once, recorded by the `gh32807-compaction-target-240k` marker. Settings raised or disabled after that migration ran (for example `aidevops astra-context disable`, `gpt6-context disable`, `gpt56-context disable`, or `runtime.opencode.v2_compaction_target`) stay in effect. Larger usable context has no cost advantage: every turn re-reads the cached context and pauses over five minutes rewrite it. Large contexts also push Codex-backend request bodies past the 1 MiB proxy limit that causes HTTP 503s.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migration-compaction-target.sh`: run the same reset once more under a new marker with its own backup, then keep honouring later explicit opt-outs.
- Keep the `setup.sh` call sites unchanged (`migrate_compaction_target_240k`).

## Acceptance

- Users who already have the GH#32807 marker but have raised settings are reset once, with a backup.
- A later explicit opt-out is honoured.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-compaction-target-migration.sh` passes.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-compaction-target-migration.sh`; ShellCheck.

body:
**Task ID:** `t18674` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): stop every worker launch scanning the whole temp root with du before model selection

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `pulse dispatch launch gap du temp root todo-sync sweep worker log setup` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open or recently merged PRs on the target files; the per-launch sweep and its `du` arrived together in GH#28860 (#28928, 2026-07-30)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main 141140ee22: `_ptsw_effective_recovery_cap` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh:436`), `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-temp-helper.sh:57`), `_dlw_setup_worker_log` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:237`), `_dlw_prebootstrap_gates` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh:488`) and the orchestrator `_dispatch_launch_worker` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1849`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — one function made lazy, one timed wrapper, two test-harness lines
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Pulse throughput investigation. Dispatch attempts lost minutes between the eligibility gate and model selection, a window with no stage records, and some of them then hit the 600s per-candidate timeout.

## What

Worker launch no longer runs a full-tree `du` of the shared temp root when the result cannot change the TODO-sync recovery cap, and the pre-model launch window (worker log setup and pre-bootstrap gates) writes entry and completion stage records.

## Why

- Every launch calls `_dlw_setup_worker_log` → `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` → `_ptsw_sweep_stale_workspaces` → `_ptsw_effective_recovery_cap`, which always ran `du -sk` over `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp`.
- That `du` result matters only when TODO-sync candidates exceed the configured cap (default 50) but stay below the count threshold (default 50). With the defaults it can never change the cap. This runner had 1 TODO-sync workspace.
- The temp root on this runner holds about 39 GiB and 30,687 top-level entries. `du -sk` took 41.2s, then 35.8s (12.2s system) at load average 130. The live `_ptsw_effective_recovery_cap` call measured 32s on the base code and 0s with this change, with the same cap (50).
- `dispatch-stages.tsv` (80 attempts since 2026-10-10): the untimed gap between `eligibility_gate` completion and `resolve_tier_model` start was p50 64.9s, p90 255.9s, max 405.5s. During 18:39–18:48Z on 2026-10-11 six attempts spent 276–406s there while the wave ran 6 candidates in parallel, each with its own `du`. At least two of them then hit the 600s per-candidate timeout (`rc=124`, `reason=launch_error`) after reaching the canary.
- The dependency check in the same window is not the cost: the same issues' `dedup.blocked_by` stage (same `is_blocked_by_unresolved` call) took 1.4–6.2s, once 20.4s.
- The window had no stage records, so a timeout kill left no evidence of where the time went.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a behaviour-preserving short-circuit in one function plus a timed wrapper around two existing calls. Dispatch-path module, so every gate keeps its order and return codes.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh:436-457` — in `_ptsw_effective_recovery_cap`, return the configured cap when `candidate_count <= cap`, return `candidate_count` when it also reaches the count threshold, and only otherwise measure temp-root usage. Results are identical for every input.
- `NEW: _dlw_timed_log_and_prebootstrap` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh` (after `_dlw_prebootstrap_gates`) — wraps `_dlw_setup_worker_log` and `_dlw_prebootstrap_gates` with `_ds_stage_start`/`_ds_record` (stages `setup_worker_log`, `prebootstrap_gates`), sets `_DLW_WORKER_LOG`, and keeps the existing `prebootstrap_gate` pre-runtime failure path.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1865-1870` — the orchestrator calls the wrapper (100 → 96 lines, under the function-complexity gate).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh:253` — stub `_ds_stage_start` beside the existing `_ds_record` stub, as other dispatch suites do.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh:18` — unset `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR` in setup. The suite inherited the caller's value, failed its sweep case, and ran delete-mode sweeps plus three full `du` scans (103.8s) against the caller's real temp root.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_ptsw_effective_recovery_cap` has one caller, `_ptsw_sweep_stale_workspaces`, reached from `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` (worker launch) and `pulse-temp-worktree-cleanup.sh:510` (cycle cleanup). `_dlw_setup_worker_log` and `_dlw_prebootstrap_gates` have one production caller each, the orchestrator.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** no change to which workspaces the sweep removes; `dispatch-stages.tsv` gains `dedup.setup_worker_log` and `dedup.prebootstrap_gates` records in the existing format.
- **Existing verification/tests:** listed below.
- **Schemas/config:** none; `PULSE_TODO_SYNC_PRESSURE_*` keep their meaning.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the commit.

### Implementation Steps

1. Short-circuit `_ptsw_effective_recovery_cap`.
2. Add the timed wrapper and call it from the orchestrator.
3. Stub `_ds_stage_start` in the precreation suite; make the temp-dir suite hermetic.
4. Run ShellCheck and the suites below on Bash 5 and `/bin/bash` 3.2.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Equivalence:** both pressure rules require `candidate_count > cap`, and the count rule wins before size is consulted. An old-versus-new comparison with a fake `du` matched on 11 cases (under/at/over cap, count and size pressure, size threshold ±1 KiB, zero candidates, invalid cap) on Bash 5 and 3.2; `du` ran only in the 4 size-pressure cases.
- **Instrumentation:** stage writes are fail-open; `_ds_stage_start` is defined wherever `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` is loaded.
- **Bash 3.2:** no new constructs.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_dispatch_launch_worker` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`
- **Current line count:** 100 lines (threshold: 100 lines for function-complexity)
- **Estimated growth:** −4 lines
- **Projected post-change:** 96 lines
- **Action required:** None — the timing lives in the new 23-line wrapper.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-todo-sync-stale-cleanup.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** the stale-cleanup suite drives the real cap under count pressure; the temp-dir suite drives the real `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` and `_dlw_setup_worker_log`; the precreation suite drives the real orchestrator.
- **Live check after release and update:** `dispatch-stages.tsv` shows `dedup.setup_worker_log` completions in seconds, and the gap between `eligibility_gate` and `resolve_tier_model` start falls well below the p50 of 64.9s.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared contract, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [x] Focused functional verification passes
- [x] WIP commit created before broad gates
- [x] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required — scoped modules

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change which workspaces the sweep removes, the cap defaults, the gate order, or the per-candidate timeout.

**Not in scope (follow-up):** leaked GitHub transport temp files in the same root (12,171 `gh-request-attempts.*`, 7,484 `gh-transport-error.*`, 7,274 `gh-transport-meta.*`; 762 entries older than 7 days). They are removed on normal exit, but nothing traps a kill and nothing reaps them later.

**AI brief owner:** interactive maintainer session that filed this task.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-sync-workspace.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18674-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The recovery cap measures temp-root usage only when candidates exceed the cap and stay below the count threshold.

  ```yaml

    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-todo-sync-stale-cleanup.sh"
  ```

  ```yaml
    prompt: "dedup.setup_worker_log completions in ~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv take seconds, not tens of seconds"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Short-circuit, not a new cache or schedule:** the size signal stays available for the one configuration where it matters.
- **Wrapper, not inline timing:** `_dispatch_launch_worker` sat at the 100-line gate.
- **Entry records:** `_ds_stage_start` keeps a killed stage attributable, which completion-only records cannot.

title: Release provenance mismatch should print expected vs observed source PRs
body:
## Observed

`aidevops release patch <pr> incremental --expected-sources <list>` failed twice with only:

```
release-provenance: observed release source manifest does not exactly match the trusted expected source set
Release preparation retained for guarded recovery (exit 1).
```

The error does not say which PRs were missing or unexpected. The operator had to read `release-snapshot-helper.sh` and replay `git rev-list --first-parent base..snapshot` by hand to find that the snapshot included the previous release-provenance merge PR (`chore(release): preserve signed vX.Y.Z publication`) and a PR merged just before it. Each failed attempt re-reserves the release lane, so every retry also waits the five-minute reserved-lane recovery window.

## Expected

On mismatch, print the expected and observed PR sets and their difference (missing, unexpected). Also offer a read-only preview that prints the observed snapshot source set before any lane reservation, for example `aidevops release sources <pr>`. Then the first `--expected-sources` attempt can be correct.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh` — `_release_provenance_assert_expected_sources` (prints the generic error). The snapshot path calls it from `_release_provenance_resolve_snapshot`.
- `.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh` — `release_snapshot_sources` (computes the observed set; reusable for a read-only preview).
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh` / `aidevops.sh` release dispatch — optional preview subcommand.

## Verification

- Unit: call `_release_provenance_assert_expected_sources` with differing sets; the stderr output names the missing and unexpected PR numbers.
- Runtime: run `aidevops release patch <pr> --expected-sources <subset>` against a range with extra PRs; the error lists them, and no tag is created.
- Constraint: the diagnostic adds no secrets and changes no trust decisions.

title: browser-qa-helper: --url with a query string gets the page path appended after the query
body:
## What happened

`browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url "https://site.local/?token=abc"` (default `--pages "/"`) loaded `https://site.local/?token=abc/`: the page path is concatenated after the query string, so the token gained a trailing `/` and the page rendered its "unavailable" state. The screenshot still reported `status: ok`.

Workaround used: `--url https://site.local --pages "/?token=abc"`.

## Where

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh` (stability script, ~line 245: `const url = baseUrl + pagePath;`)
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh` (screenshot capture, which prints "Capturing screenshots for"); same join pattern expected.

## Fix

Join with `new URL(pagePath, baseUrl)` semantics, or when `--url` already has a query or fragment and `--pages` was left at its default, load `--url` as given. Apply it to every command that joins base URL and page (screenshot, smoke, a11y, stability, links).

## Verify

`browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url "https://example.com/?q=1"` loads exactly `https://example.com/?q=1`, and `--url https://example.com --pages "/a /b"` still loads `/a` and `/b`. Run ShellCheck on the edited scripts.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: fix(pulse): complexity scan never runs because it git-pulls the guarded canonical checkout
body:
## What

Make the Pulse complexity scan read current `origin/main` without mutating the canonical aidevops checkout, so the scan runs again.

## Why

- `_complexity_scan_pull_latest` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh:605-633`) runs `git -C <canonical aidevops checkout> pull --ff-only --no-rebase` before every scan and fails closed when the pull fails.
- The canonical Git guard blocks that pull: `BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git pull'`. The helper then logs `Complexity scan: git pull failed for <path> — skipping this cycle to avoid stale-state warnings` and returns 1.
- Retained `pulse.log` on one runner (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-11): 58 guard blocks, 58 skip lines, 0 completed scans. The scan produces no findings while this holds.
- Bypassing the guard is not acceptable. Canonical checkouts are read-only service mirrors (`reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`), and the guard exists to stop exactly this mutation.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh:605-633` — replace the pull with a read-only refresh: fetch `origin main`, then materialise `origin/main` into a temporary directory (for example `git archive origin/main | tar -x -C "$tmp"`, or a detached temporary worktree that is removed afterwards) and return that path.
- `EDIT:` the caller(s) of `_complexity_scan_pull_latest` in the same file — pass the returned path to the scan steps that read working-tree files (the proximity guard and the tree-change check named in the GH#17848 comment), and remove the temporary tree when the scan ends, including on failure.
- Find every reader with `rg -n '_complexity_scan_pull_latest|aidevops_path' .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh`.

### Reference pattern

- Temporary paths: `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}` with `mktemp -d` and a cleanup trap, as in other pulse helpers.
- Keep the existing fail-closed behaviour: if fetch or export fails, skip the cycle without updating `COMPLEXITY_SCAN_LAST_RUN`, as today.
- Keep the existing `timeout_sec 30` network bound on the fetch.

## Verification

1. With the canonical checkout behind `origin/main`, run the scan stage. Confirm `git -C <canonical> rev-parse HEAD` and `git -C <canonical> status --porcelain` are unchanged afterwards.
2. Confirm the scan read `origin/main` content (for example, a file present only on `origin/main` is counted).
3. Confirm `pulse.log` shows a completed scan, with no `git pull failed` line and no canonical-guard block.
4. Confirm the temporary tree is removed after success and after an injected failure.
5. `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-scan.sh` is clean. Run the existing suites found by `rg -l 'complexity_scan|simplification-scan' .agents/scripts/tests/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The complexity scan completes on a runner whose canonical checkout is guarded, without any canonical worktree mutation.
- No guard bypass, `--no-verify`, or guard allowlist change.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: fix(runner-capability): fixed 5s secret-check timeout defers dispatch on loaded runners
body:
## What

Stop the runner-capability secret check from reporting `check_timeout` on a healthy but loaded runner. Make its fixed 5-second timeout configurable, with a default that covers measured loaded-host latency.

## Why

- `run_check` in the embedded Python of `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:106` waits `timeout=5` for `aidevops secret check <NAME>`, then kills the process group and returns `check_timeout <target>`.
- The dispatcher treats that as `runner_capability_unmet reason=check_timeout` and defers the candidate. Retained `pulse.log` on one runner holds 13 such deferrals (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-11). All were QA credentials required by enrichment-class issues in a managed private repo, and each deferral came after the full per-candidate dedup ceremony (tens of seconds) had already run.
- The secrets were present. A direct `aidevops secret check` measured 0.7–1.6s at load average 35–70 on 16 cores, but this runner regularly runs at load 100–150, where the 5s bound is exceeded.
- `cooldown=none` means the issue is retried on the next cycle, but that wave slot is lost each time.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:106` — read the secret-check timeout from an environment variable (for example `AIDEVOPS_RUNNER_CAPABILITY_SECRET_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), default 15, clamped to 1–60, invalid values falling back to the default. Keep the process-group kill on expiry.
- `EDIT:` the other `run_check` call sites in the same file (`rg -n 'run_check\(' .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`) — leave probe and SSH timeouts unchanged unless evidence shows the same problem. The network-policy check already uses `AIDEVOPS_NETWORK_POLICY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (`:271`), which is the reference pattern.
- If the helper documents its environment variables in its usage text or a reference doc, add the new variable there.

## Verification

1. Point the helper at a stub `aidevops` that sleeps 8s and then exits 0. Before: `check_timeout`. After: met with the default.
2. Set the timeout variable to 2 and confirm the same stub returns `check_timeout`.
3. Confirm the process-group kill still removes a stub that spawns a long-running child.
4. `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh` is clean. Run the existing suites from `rg -l 'runner-capability' .agents/scripts/tests/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A present secret whose check finishes within the default bound under load is reported as met.
- Missing and unreadable secrets still return `secret_missing`/`secret_unreadable` with no added delay.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: fix(pulse): parallel dispatch starts candidate stages below the 600s per-candidate floor
body:
## What

Stop parallel dispatch from starting a candidate's `dispatch_with_dedup` stage with less than the per-candidate ceremony floor (600s) left in the cycle. Re-check the floor where the stage starts. If the budget is short, defer the candidate without recording a launch failure.

## Why

- The parallel loop `_dispatch_max_loop` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:814-863`) checks the cycle budget against the floor in `_dispatch_max_should_stop` → `_dispatch_graphql_budget_allows_next` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:802-812`) before it spawns `_dispatch_max_spawn_candidate` in the background.
- The spawned candidate then runs its pre-stage checks in `_dispatch_process_candidate` before `_dispatch_with_timeout` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:546-603`) calls `run_stage_with_timeout`. That call clamps the stage timeout to the remaining cycle budget in `_pulse_stage_cycle_timeout` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:220-234`). Under load, the pre-stage work took about 200s.
- Observed in one wave (2026-10-11 ~18:00Z): iterations 1–2 passed the floor check, and iteration 3 logged `Dispatch_max stopping early: cycle wall-clock budget below per-candidate floor (remaining=580s floor=600s)`. The 4 candidates already admitted then logged `Stage cycle budget clamp: dispatch_candidate_<N> 1200s -> 380s/373s/354s/350s`. One was killed at its 380s clamp after it had won its claim (`rc=124`, `pre-launch failure ... reason=launch_error`).
- Retained `pulse.log` on that runner (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-11): 37 `Stage start: dispatch_candidate_<N> (timeout <600s)` lines, 7 of them at 330–472s.
- GH#33560 (closed) fixed the admission-time variant. This is the remaining path between admission and stage start.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:546-603` (`_dispatch_with_timeout`) — after computing `timeout_seconds` (adaptive value raised to the floor), read `_pulse_cycle_remaining_seconds "${AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CYCLE_FINALISE_RESERVE_S:-90}"`. If that is below `DISPATCH_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT_FLOOR` (default 600), log one `Dispatch_max: deferring #N — cycle budget <remaining>s below per-candidate floor` line and return a distinct non-failure code, without calling `run_stage_with_timeout`. Keep the fail-open behaviour when the remaining-seconds helper is unavailable.
- `EDIT:` the outcome mapping for that code (`_dispatch_record_candidate_outcome`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:1061`, and the pre-launch failure classification that logs `reason=launch_error`) — record it as a deferral, not a launch failure, so it does not feed fast-fail or backoff counters.

title: test(pulse): make test-dispatch-min-concurrency independent of live host CPU load
body:
## What

Make `test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh` independent of the host's live CPU load. Its capacity cases read the real CPU admission gate and fail on a busy runner.

## Why

- The suite sources `pulse-capacity.sh` and calls `_dispatch_compute_capacity`, which reaches `_pulse_cpu_pressure` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:388-418`). That function reads the real one-minute load average and core count, and samples real `iostat` idle when load exceeds the threshold. A closed gate forces `max_workers=0`.
- On a runner at load 138 on 16 cores (idle below 25%), 10 of 31 cases failed with results such as `result=0 2 0 floor_active=0` (expected `6 2 4`). The failures included `capacity: raises max_workers to floor while active below floor` and `apply: refills minimum active-worker floor after partial launch`.
- With `MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE=1000` set (gate forced open), the same tree passed 31/31. The failures come from the environment, not the code under test.
- Workers run this suite on loaded shared runners. A false failure there wastes worker time and produces misleading "pre-existing failure" reports. CI hosts are quiet, so CI does not catch it.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh:51-60` — after sourcing the pulse modules, give the capacity cases a deterministic open CPU gate. Either define a `_pulse_cpu_pressure` stub that prints an open gate (for example `1.00 16 open 4.0 na`), or set the load and idle mocks the way `test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh` does (`sysctl`/`iostat` shims driven by `MOCK_LOAD`/`MOCK_IDLE`, lines 62-114). Cases that need a closed gate should set it explicitly.
- `CHECK:` other suites that reach `_dispatch_compute_capacity` or `calculate_max_workers` without mocking CPU telemetry: `rg -l '_dispatch_compute_capacity|calculate_max_workers' .agents/scripts/tests/`, then compare with `rg -l '_pulse_cpu_pressure|MOCK_LOAD' .agents/scripts/tests/`. Fix any with the same live dependency in this PR. List them in the PR body if there are none.

### Reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh:62-136` — CPU telemetry mocks.

3. Run it with `/bin/bash` 3.2 if the suite supports it, and with Bash 5.
4. `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh` is clean.

## Acceptance criteria

title: fix(pulse): merged-partial continuation never revisits in-review chain heads whose worker lease expired
body:
## What

Give merged-partial continuation (GH#34312) a second chance once the worker's dispatch lease has expired. Today the decision runs once, at merge time. If the newest owner event then is a non-terminal `DISPATCH_LEASE`, the issue stays `status:in-review`, keeps its runner assignee and lacks `auto-dispatch`, with no open PR and nothing that revisits it.

## Why

- `_pmpc_release_owner_from_comments` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh:147-176`) returns "live" for any newest non-terminal `DISPATCH_LEASE` and ignores `expires_at`. The caller then logs `kept #N in review after partial PR #M — newest owner is not a finished worker run or continuation already recorded (GH#34312)` (`:404`).
- The module runs only from the deterministic merge path (`pulse-merge.sh` → `_handle_post_merge_actions`). The issue has lost `auto-dispatch`, so dispatch-time stale recovery (`dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`) never sees it either.
- Ready leases last `DISPATCH_READY_LEASE_TTL` (7200s, `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:62`). Claim consensus already treats expired generations as inactive (`dispatch-claim-helper.sh:1591-1592`), so the continuation decision disagrees with the claim protocol.
- Observed twice on 2026-10-11 in a managed private repo, both on another runner's worker (aidevops 3.39.15). The worker's `For #N` partial PR merged and the newest owner event was `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready ... expires_at=<T>`, with no `CLAIM_RELEASED` and no terminal lease. In one case the lease expired 51 minutes after the merge, and the chain head stayed stuck until a manual recovery 2h40m after the merge (1h50m after expiry). Each stuck head also blocks the rest of its enrichment chain.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh:147-176` — when the newest trusted owner event is a non-terminal `DISPATCH_LEASE` whose `expires_at` parses and is older than `now - grace` (grace default 900s, env-tunable), return `released:<lease author>`, the same verdict as a terminal lease. Keep every other rule unchanged: `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_ownership_lost` stays live, any later `DISPATCH_CLAIM`, `Dispatching worker` or interactive claim stays live, and unreadable data fails closed.
- `NEW:` a bounded periodic pass, reusing the module's existing guards (`_pmpc_issue_scope`, `_pmpc_owned_assignees`, `_pmpc_other_open_pr_owns_issue`, `_pmpc_pr_body_has_closing_ref`, marker idempotency) and its projection (`_pmpc_project_available` plus `_pmpc_post_audit_comment`). It covers open issues labelled `status:in-review` with no open linked PR, whose newest linked merged PR is a non-closing `For`/`Ref` partial. Attach it to an existing per-repo cadence that already reads issue comments, such as the stale-blocked reconciliation stage, and cap it per cycle like that stage's budget.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` — add fixture cases to the existing suite: an expired ready lease releases; an unexpired ready lease stays live; an expired lease followed by a newer `DISPATCH_CLAIM` stays live; a missing or malformed `expires_at` stays live.

### Reference pattern

- Lease parsing: `expires_at=<epoch>` fields as written by `dispatch-claim-helper.sh`. Existing fixtures in `tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:658-686` show the comment shapes.
- Idempotent audit marker `<!-- aidevops:ops kind=merged-partial-recovery ... -->`, already produced by the module.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`

Integration: the existing per-repo stale-blocked cadence in pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh supplies the periodic pass and deadline. Verification also runs the existing stale-blocked reconciliation suite.

## Verification

1. Suite: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh` passes on Bash 5 and `/bin/bash` 3.2, including the new cases.
2. Dry run of the periodic pass, with writes stubbed (the suite's existing approach), against a repo holding one expired-lease zombie and one live lease: only the expired case is projected to `status:available` (+`auto-dispatch` for leaves), and its assignee is released.
3. A second run is a no-op (marker idempotency).
4. `shellcheck -x` is clean on the changed files.

## Acceptance criteria

- A merged-partial chain head whose worker lease expired more than the grace period ago returns to `status:available` within one periodic pass, without manual cleanup.
- No change for live leases, held issues (`hold-for-review`, `needs-*`, `no-auto-dispatch`), parent trackers (unassign only, as today) or issues with an open PR.

title: Release reconcile cannot claim preserved local tag when lane is reconcile-required (silent exit 75)
body:
## Observed

After a failed release push (cause: repo-verify pre-push block, see sibling issue), the release lane for source PR #34420 is:

```
RELEASE_LANE={"active":true,"source_pr":34420,"phase":"reconcile-required","tag":null,...,"terminal_receipt":null}
RELEASE_EXECUTOR={"state": "dead", "reason": "process-absent"}
RELEASE_RECEIPT=failed
Protected release PR is not yet queued for preserved v3.39.20
```

A signed local tag `v3.39.20` exists (release commit `7f06c24bee`, parent = snapshot `6753807dac`). No remote tag, no `chore/release-v3.39.20-provenance` branch and no protected release PR exist. `aidevops release reconcile 34420` exits 75 with no further output. `aidevops release patch 34420` refuses with "reconcile instead of creating another version bump".

## Cause (from reading the code)

`full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` `_full_loop_release_reconcile_protected_state` correctly reaches the `pr-missing` → `_full_loop_release_queue_preserved_tag` path, but `_full_loop_release_claim_preserved_tag` only accepts lane phase `preparing` (tag null) or `remote-publication` (with `preserved_tag_recovery`). The helper wrote `reconcile-required` on failure (`full-loop-release-helper.sh` ~line 536, `release_lane_update ... "reconcile-required"`), so the claim's jq predicate fails and the function `return 75`s. This state has no automatic exit.

## Expected

When the lane is `reconcile-required`, the tag is null, the executor is dead, a signed local tag with matching snapshot parent and authorization exists, and all publication channels are absent, reconcile should claim the preserved tag (same CAS/fencing as the `preparing` case) and queue the protected release PR. Otherwise it should print a precise reason and the next command instead of a silent 75.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` `_full_loop_release_claim_preserved_tag` (phase predicate around line 153-167)
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh` failure path that writes `reconcile-required` (~line 536)
- `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh` phase constants
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-supersession.sh`, `test-release-lane.sh` patterns

## Verification

- Unit: a lane in `reconcile-required` with a dead executor and a valid preserved local tag is claimed and queued; a live executor or mismatched authorization still returns 75 with a printed reason.
- Runtime: `aidevops release reconcile 34420` queues the v3.39.20 protected release PR once the sibling repo-verify fix is deployed.

title: Release pushes blocked by repo-verify pre-push in dependency-free release worktrees
body:
## Observed

`aidevops release patch 34420 incremental --expected-sources ...` built and signed v3.39.20 locally (bump commit `7f06c24bee`). Every release push was then blocked by the `repo-verify` pre-push guard:

```
[repo-verify][INFO] running typecheck: bun run typecheck
bash: line 1: tsc: command not found
[repo-verify][BLOCK] typecheck could not start: missing JavaScript dev dependencies
```

Reproduced with `git push --dry-run origin <merge-head>:refs/heads/chore/release-v3.39.20-provenance` from the retained release worktree. The direct `main` push attempts and the protected recovery-branch push (`Could not publish protected release recovery branch` / `Git rejected the recovery branch push`) both fail before reaching GitHub.

## Cause

The release helper creates detached release/tag worktrees (`aidevops-release-<pr>-<pid>`, `aidevops-release-reconcile-<ver>-<pid>` under the worktree base dir) without `node_modules`. #34412 (GH: install pre-push guards in the effective `core.hooksPath`) now installs the guard chain into `.beads/hooks` in this repo; the hook file timestamp shows it went active minutes before this release. So this is the first release that runs `repo-verify` (`bun run typecheck`) inside a dependency-free release worktree. v3.39.19 published before that change.

## Expected

Release-tool pushes carry only version-file bumps and provenance merges on top of CI-verified `main`, so they must not depend on JS dev dependencies in the release worktree. Pick one, with the reasoning in the PR:

1. Narrow (preferred): the release pushes in `version-manager-git.sh` (`git push --atomic origin HEAD:refs/heads/main --tags`) and `version-manager-protected-main.sh` (recovery-branch push, preserved-tag push) set `AIDEVOPS_PREPUSH_REPO_VERIFY=0` for that one command only. Privacy, complexity, credential and scope guards keep running. Add `#aidevops:trust-boundary` with the rationale.
2. Or provision the release worktree through `worktree-js-readiness-helper.sh prepare` before the first push, if that is fast and has no network dependency.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/version-manager-git.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/version-manager-protected-main.sh`

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-git.sh` around `push_changes` (`git push --atomic origin HEAD:refs/heads/main --tags`)
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-protected-main.sh` `_version_manager_prepare_protected_release_head` (recovery-branch push) and the preserved-tag push (`refs/tags/${tag_name}:refs/tags/${tag_name}`)
- `.agents/hooks/repo-verify-pre-push.sh` (reference only; skip conditions are documented at the top)
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-protected-main-fallback.sh` pattern

## Verification

- From a dependency-free detached worktree with the managed guard chain active, the release push paths reach GitHub (or their stubs) and the privacy/complexity guards still run.
- `shellcheck` clean; existing version-manager protected-main tests pass.
- Then resume the stuck v3.39.20 release lane (see sibling issue for the `reconcile-required` lane claim).

title: full-loop merge: review-only admin fallback refuses when branch protection has no required checks (none=0)
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <repo>` (without `--admin`) on a repo whose branch protection requires one approving review and **no** required status checks:

1. Remote PR evidence logs `no required checks are configured`, and the review-bot gate passes.

When branch protection has no required status checks (verified from the protection API, not inferred from an empty rollup), the fallback's required-check re-read should classify the state as clear (`no-required`). Interactive maintainer sessions can then take the documented review-only admin path without a manual `--admin`.

A related question: the plain-merge error text was the generic "base branch policy prohibits the merge" message, not "At least N approving review". Confirm that `_merge_try_review_only_admin_fallback` still identifies a review-only block in that case. Keep it fail-closed for any other policy.

title: t18675: fix(pulse): stop setup reconciliation killing in-flight Pulse cycles on every...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18675` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): stop setup reconciliation killing in-flight Pulse cycles on every deploy

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `pulse reconcile-managed setup deploy kills in-flight cycle drain` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open or recently merged PRs on `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` beyond GH#33777 (#33784, watchdog revive loop); issue searches for reconcile/interrupted-cycle duplicates returned nothing
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main 0b77031120: `_reconcile_managed` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh:858`), `_stop_reconciliation_processes` (`:726`), `_pulse_start_managed` (`:272`), `_pulse_pid_uses_active_runtime` (`:504`), `_pulse_pids` (`:617`), `_setup_restart_pulse_if_running` (`setup.sh:1976`, called unconditionally from `setup.sh:2115`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — one decision function in the lifecycle helper plus fixture coverage in the existing deploy suite
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Pulse throughput investigation. Interrupted cycles were the largest single loss of dispatch time on this runner, and every interrupted record lined up with the end of a setup run.

## What

Setup's Pulse reconciliation no longer kills a launchd-managed Pulse cycle that is still running from an earlier runtime bundle. The cycle finishes on its own bundle and launchd starts the activated bundle at the next start. A cycle older than a drain ceiling (default 3600s) is still replaced immediately, as today.

## Why

- Every `setup.sh` run ends with `_setup_restart_pulse_if_running` → `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh reconcile-managed`, including scoped `--stage` runs. `_stop_reconciliation_processes` snapshots every `pulse-wrapper.sh` / `pulse-merge-routine.sh` process regardless of the bundle it runs, sends TERM, waits 2s, escalates to KILL, then `launchctl kickstart -k`.
- On 2026-10-11 (UTC) this runner recorded 39 cycles in `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`: 9 `progressed` (16 workers dispatched), 13 `idle`, 17 `partial/interrupted` (4 dispatched). All 17 interrupted records were written 2–16s after a setup run's last timed stage (`setup_tabby` in `setup-stage-timings.log`), i.e. at the reconciliation step. They had run 17–1,566s; 10,605s of cycle wall time was discarded that day.
- There were 42 setup runs that day. `auto-update.log` alone shows 22 "Stopping pre-reconciliation Pulse process(es)" events, 19 escalated to SIGKILL; three of them redeployed the commit the killed cycle was already running (same `<version>-<sha>` bundle prefix).
- Productive cycles take long on this runner: progressed cycles ran 1,717–2,296s wall (max 2,445s over two days), and dispatch happens late in the cycle, so a deploy landing mid-cycle usually throws away the dispatch it was about to make.
- Killing is not needed for code consistency. A running cycle executes one immutable bundle: `pulse-wrapper.sh` resolves its physical script directory and holds a runtime-bundle lease (`pulse-wrapper.sh:204-233`), and old bundles stay on disk while leased. The supervisor LaunchAgent runs the stable link `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` with `StartInterval` 120 and `KeepAlive`/`SuccessfulExit=false`, so the next start after the cycle exits resolves to the activated bundle.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a guarded early exit in one lifecycle function, with the immediate path unchanged; correctness hinges on process classification already implemented in the helper.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — add `_pulse_process_age_seconds` (portable `ps -o etime=` parser; macOS `ps` has no `etimes`), `_pulse_launchd_supervisor_loaded` (`launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>` succeeds), and `_pulse_reconcile_defers_to_cycle_boundary`. In `_reconcile_managed`, between the supervisor-disabled branch and the stop/start branch, add `elif _pulse_reconcile_defers_to_cycle_boundary; then` that retires only standalone merge routines (`_stop_reconciliation_processes standalone-merge`, selected through `_pulse_pid_descends_from`) and does not kickstart launchd. Document `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_RECONCILE_DRAIN` and `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_RECONCILE_DRAIN_MAX_AGE_S` in the header and `_usage`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh` — fixture cases with the existing fake `launchctl`: an earlier-bundle cycle under the ceiling and the merge routine it spawned are left running with no `kickstart`, while a standalone merge routine is retired; the same cycle with the ceiling at 0 is replaced by the active bundle through `kickstart -k`.

### Decision rules

`_pulse_reconcile_defers_to_cycle_boundary` returns 1 (keep today's immediate replacement) when any of these hold:

1. `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_RECONCILE_DRAIN=0`;
2. the launchd supervisor job is not loaded (Linux, cron/systemd, manual starts keep today's behaviour);
3. no main Pulse PID is running (`_pulse_pids` empty — nothing to lose, start now);
4. any earlier-bundle main PID has an unreadable age or an age at or above the ceiling.

Otherwise it logs which PIDs keep running and returns 0. Main PIDs already proven to run the activated bundle (`_pulse_pid_uses_active_runtime`) are reported as current and never signalled.

Merge routines are split by process tree. One spawned inside a cycle (`pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh:176`, `${SCRIPT_DIR}/pulse-merge-routine.sh`) runs from that cycle's leased bundle and finishes with it. The standalone launchd job runs the stable link (`schedulers-platform.sh:455`), and `pulse-merge-routine.sh:54` resolves `SCRIPT_DIR` without `pwd -P` and takes no lease, so after activation it would call new-bundle helpers from old in-memory code. It is still retired while a cycle drains; its 60s job restarts it on the activated bundle.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `reconcile-managed` is called only by `_restart_pulse_if_running` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh:17`), from `setup.sh:2022`. `stop`, `restart`, `restart-if-running`, and the supervisor-disabled path are unchanged.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** while a cycle drains, only standalone merge routines are signalled and launchd is not kickstarted; no files written.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh`, `test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`, `test-pulse-launchd-setup.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** two optional environment knobs; no config schema change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/`; setup runs the activated bundle's helper, so the release that ships this fix already reconciles with it.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_RECONCILE_DRAIN=0`, or revert the commit.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Convergence:** an earlier-bundle cycle keeps running for at most the ceiling after the first deferring setup; the next setup after that replaces it. Operators who need new code immediately still run `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart`.
- **Single instance:** launchd does not start a second instance of the job while the cycle runs, so deferral cannot create two top-level revisions of the main Pulse (GH#27885 acceptance).
- **Bootstrap recovery:** `pulse-runtime-recovery.sh` runs `setup.sh --stage ai-session` from inside a starting wrapper; that wrapper is young, so it now defers instead of terminating itself before the recovery re-exec.
- **Bash 3.2:** here-strings, pattern substitution and `10#` arithmetic only.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-deploy-pulse-runtime.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-launchd-setup.sh
```
